items.stem: Ice Giant of mass 6.32 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Retrograde Moon of mass 7.8 × 10²² kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) form a Neptune–Triton-analog planetary pair separated centre-to-centre by 3.66 × 10⁸ m. Calculate the distance from Ice Giant's centre to the collinear gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: From the airless surface of Primary Planet (mass 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m), a cislunar transfer probe is fired along the line of centres toward Companion Moon (mass 1.67 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) at separation 2.92 × 10⁸ m. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², determine the threshold launch speed to cross the null-point barrier.
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -7.40 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 2.50 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -1.87 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 7.21 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.20 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.20 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a sub-Neptune and its massive exomoon separated by 3.54 × 10⁸ m between centres, Primary has mass 7.27 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Exomoon has mass 1.48 × 10²³ kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m). Referencing potential to zero at infinity and taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate V_g at the gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.10 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -1.79 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -1.79 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: In a Pluto–Charon-type dwarf-planet binary of centre-to-centre separation 4.88 × 10⁸ m, a 2220 kg New-Horizons-class flyby craft crosses the line of centres 2.2 × 10⁸ m from Dwarf Planet A (9.47 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) toward Companion B (5.92 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m). Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate |g_net|.
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.0131 − 5.50 × 10⁻⁴| = 0.0125 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.0125 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in a double-planetesimal binary system — Body Alpha (1.13 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (1.81 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) — lie 5.69 × 10⁸ m apart between centres. How far from Body Alpha's centre do their gravitational fields cancel?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 4.06 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 4.06 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: Along the 5.01 × 10⁸ m line of centres of a Pluto–Charon-type dwarf-planet binary, Dwarf Planet A (1.32 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Companion B (1.47 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) create a zero-field saddle point. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², find the total gravitational potential there.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.76 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -3.13 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -3.13 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the least initial speed at Primary Asteroid's surface (1.64 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) enabling a ballistic ion-beam shepherd craft to reach Secondary Moonlet (1.03 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) across a 6.05 × 10⁸ m centre-to-centre baseline (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -1.72 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 4.84 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -2.83 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.69 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.84 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.84 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Between Primary Planet (mass 3.79 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Companion Moon (mass 1.05 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m), whose centres are 7.51 × 10⁸ m apart, find the combined gravitational field strength at a 978 kg cislunar transfer probe located 2.63 × 10⁸ m from Primary Planet's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.00365 − 2.94 × 10⁻⁵| = 0.00363 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.00363 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A 1200 kg scientific transit module coasts along the axis connecting Planet Major (mass 8.95 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Planet Minor (mass 3.58 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) in a terrestrial bi-planetary system of centre-to-centre separation 4.61 × 10⁸ m, crossing coordinate x = 2.86 × 10⁸ m from Planet Major's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.84 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 2.86 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00652 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 7.82 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 7.82 N.

workingSteps: Equating field magnitudes gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 2.50 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined gravitational potential at this null point.
workingSteps: V(x₀) = −G M₁ / x₀ − G M₂ / (d − x₀) = -5.25 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the minimum launch speed from the surface of Ice Giant along the line of centres required for a deep-space relay probe to reach Retrograde Moon.
workingSteps: ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.44 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹; v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.70 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 0.75 kg human-rated centrifuge gondola revolves at a constant speed of 3.08 m s⁻¹ in a vertical circle of radius 0.65 m guided by a rigid rotating arm. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both tension and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.75 × ((3.08)² / 0.65 − 9.81) = 3.59 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 3.59 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 15.1 N.

items.stem: An unpowered 0.35 kg hardened steel ball bearing enters the bottom of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 1.6 m at 10.3 m s⁻¹ under energy-conserving conditions (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What normal contact force acts on it at the apex?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (10.3)² − 4(9.81)(1.6) = 43.3 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.35(43.3 / 1.6 − 9.81) = 6.04 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 6.04 N.

items.stem: A 0.5 kg low-friction maglev test sled currently enters a vertical circular guide ring of radius 4.2 m at 17.5 m s⁻¹ under frictionless conditions (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the critical minimum speed at the bottom required to just clear the apex.
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 4.2) = 14.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Calculate the road normal reaction on a 1350 kg vintage touring car cresting the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of radius 38 m at constant speed 16.6 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1350 × (9.81 − (16.6)² / 38) = 3.45 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 3.45 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Climbing a full vertical circular arc of radius 1.2 m from a bottom speed of 10.4 m s⁻¹ without energy loss (g = 9.8 m s⁻²), what normal contact force does a 1.8 kg pendulum impact bob experience at the summit?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (10.4)² − 4(9.8)(1.2) = 61.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 1.8(61.1 / 1.2 − 9.8) = 74.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 74.0 N.

items.stem: Moving at 8.08 m s⁻¹ over a convex circular ridge crest of circular radius 22 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²), what normal force supports a 650 kg autonomous rover chassis at the crest?

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 4.44 × 10³ N.

items.stem: A 3.5 kg acrobatic drone tether pod revolves at a constant speed of 4.01 m s⁻¹ in a vertical circle of radius 1.1 m guided by a constant-speed vertical line. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both tension and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 3.5 × ((4.01)² / 1.1 − 9.81) = 16.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 16.8 N.

items.stem: An unpowered precision titanium sphere of mass 45 kg enters the bottom of a polished vertical circular chute of radius 9 m with speed 31.9 m s⁻¹. Mechanical energy is conserved; take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is its speed at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((31.9)² − 4 × 9.8 × 9) = 25.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 25.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Moving without friction or propulsion, a 240 kg gravity-fed capsule car passes the lowest point of a circular vertical inversion loop (radius 0.6 m) at 5.97 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². Determine the normal contact force acting on it at the highest point.
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (5.97)² − 4(9.81)(0.6) = 12.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 240(12.1 / 0.6 − 9.81) = 2.48 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 2.48 × 10³ N.

items.stem: In a vertical whirl boom of radius 0.85 m, a 0.4 kg aerospace g-tolerance capsule rotates vertically at 4.22 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², if the drive is slowed, at what critical apex speed does the tension vanish?
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, tension = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.81 × 0.85) = 2.89 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 2.89 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular stator ring of radius 1.6 m shows a 0.75 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 6.26 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.75 × ((6.26)² / 1.6 − 9.8) = 11.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 11.0 N.

items.stem: At the base of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 9 m, an unpowered 0.2 kg hardened steel ball bearing has horizontal speed 25.6 m s⁻¹. Neglecting resistive losses and taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², find its speed at the top of the loop.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((25.6)² − 4 × 9.81 × 9) = 17.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: With negligible drag, a 0.206 kg low-friction maglev test sled sweeps through the bottom of a vertical circular guide ring (radius 0.463 m) at 6.1 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², calculate the normal contact force at the top of the circle.
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (6.1)² − 4(9.8)(0.463) = 19.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.206(19.1 / 0.463 − 9.8) = 6.46 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 6.46 N.

items.stem: Operators gradually reduce the speed of a 1.6 kg motorized whirling calibration mass from 5.34 m s⁻¹ on a taut Kevlar cord of vertical radius 0.85 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the minimum speed at the top before slackness or lift-off occurs.
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, tension = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.8 × 0.85) = 2.89 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 2.89 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An unpowered pendulum impact bob of mass 0.823 kg enters the bottom of a full vertical circular arc of radius 6.69 m with speed 26.1 m s⁻¹. Mechanical energy is conserved; take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is its speed at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((26.1)² − 4 × 9.8 × 6.69) = 20.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 20.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 2.8 m at steady speed 7.02 m s⁻¹, a 2.2 kg instrumented acrylic sphere is constrained by a vertical circular guide rail (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward normal contact force.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward normal contact force opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 2.2 × ((7.02)² / 2.8 + 9.8) = 60.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 60.3 N.

items.stem: At the summit of the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of vertical radius 18 m, a 960 kg vintage touring car moves horizontally at 11.4 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Determine the normal force exerted by the surface.
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 960 × (9.81 − (11.4)² / 18) = 2.49 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 2.49 × 10³ N.

items.stem: In a test run on a polished vertical circular chute of radius 1.23 m, a 1.23 kg precision titanium sphere enters the bottom at 8.54 m s⁻¹ with negligible friction (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the minimum bottom entry speed that would still allow it to complete the full vertical loop without losing contact at the top?
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 1.23) = 7.76 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Coasting without friction, a 46.3 kg gravity-fed capsule car passes the lowest point of a circular vertical inversion loop (radius 4.32 m) at 16.9 m s⁻¹ where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed as it crosses the apex.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((16.9)² − 4 × 9.81 × 4.32) = 10.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 10.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At the nadir of a constant-speed vertical line (vertical radius 0.65 m), a 0.55 kg acrobatic drone tether pod travels horizontally at 4.34 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what tension acts upward?
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward tension opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.55 × ((4.34)² / 0.65 + 9.81) = 21.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 21.3 N.

items.stem: Operators gradually reduce the speed of a 0.55 kg laboratory brass cylinder from 6.73 m s⁻¹ on an enclosed vertical circular hoop of vertical radius 1.35 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the minimum speed at the top before slackness or lift-off occurs.
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, normal contact force = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.8 × 1.35) = 3.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 3.64 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: For an unpowered 123 kg hardened steel ball bearing on a smooth vertical loop track of vertical radius 0.875 m (operating entry speed 8.39 m s⁻¹, g = 9.81 m s⁻²), find the least bottom speed needed so normal contact force does not vanish before the top.
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.81 × 0.875) = 6.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Conserving mechanical energy throughout a vertical circular guide ring of radius 1.65 m, a 370 kg low-friction maglev test sled enters at the bottom with speed 12.1 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Determine the speed at the summit of the loop.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((12.1)² − 4 × 9.8 × 1.65) = 9.04 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 9.04 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 1.1 m at steady speed 4.4 m s⁻¹, a 0.9 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled is constrained by a vertical circular stator ring (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward normal contact force.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward normal contact force opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.9 × ((4.4)² / 1.1 + 9.8) = 24.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 24.7 N.

items.stem: An unpowered frictionless coaster bogie of mass 0.35 kg enters the bottom of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 0.6 m with horizontal speed 5.96 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 3.46 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 3.57 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 5.42 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the string tension acting on the frictionless coaster bogie at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: Motorized drive control keeps a 0.75 kg mass moving at constant tangential speed 5.56 m s⁻¹ around a vertical circular path of radius 1.4 m using an inextensible tether. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Critical apex speed v_min = √(gR) = 3.71 m s⁻¹. (b) At the top, F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 9.20 N. (c) At the bottom, F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 23.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Sets support force to zero at apex so mg = m v_min² / R.
Subtracts mg from m v² / R at the top.
Adds mg to m v² / R at the bottom.

items.stem: An Olympic track cyclist of mass 160 kg rounds a Siberian-pine velodrome banking of horizontal radius 32 m banked at 16 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 32 × tan 16°) = 9.48 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 16°) to obtain 9.48 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 0.55 kg human-rated centrifuge gondola revolves at a constant speed of 3.52 m s⁻¹ in a vertical circle of radius 0.85 m guided by a rigid rotating arm. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both tension and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.55 × ((3.52)² / 0.85 − 9.81) = 2.62 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 2.62 N.

items.stem: Outside a spherical icy outer-system dwarf world (mass 1.49 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 4.46 × 10⁶ m), a 150 kg cryobot instrument package sits at distance 6.24 × 10⁶ m from the centre. With V_g = 0 at infinity and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate the gravitational potential there.
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.49 × 10²⁴) / 6.24 × 10⁶ = -1.59 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -1.59 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: In a Neptune–Triton-analog planetary pair separated by 2.69 × 10⁸ m between centres, Ice Giant has mass 4.18 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Retrograde Moon has mass 4.64 × 10²³ kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m). Referencing potential to zero at infinity and taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate V_g at the gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.02 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -1.84 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -1.84 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Inside a fairground swing carousel, a 1.4 m suspension wire supports a 0.6 kg gondola whirling at a steady semi-vertical cone angle of 42 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the tangential speed of the gondola.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.4 sin 42° = 0.937 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.937 × tan 42°) = 2.88 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.88 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 1.35 m at steady speed 4.87 m s⁻¹, a 0.75 kg motorized whirling calibration mass is constrained by a taut Kevlar cord (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward tension.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward tension opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.75 × ((4.87)² / 1.35 + 9.8) = 20.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 20.5 N.

items.stem: An unpowered 0.35 kg hardened steel ball bearing enters the bottom of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 1.2 m at 8.9 m s⁻¹ under energy-conserving conditions (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What normal contact force acts on it at the apex?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (8.9)² − 4(9.81)(1.2) = 32.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.35(32.1 / 1.2 − 9.81) = 5.94 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 5.94 N.

items.stem: From the surface of a non-rotating airless cratered terrestrial dwarf planet of mass 2.69 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 8.28 × 10⁶ m (monitored by a 240 kg polar radar surveyor at r = 1.45 × 10⁷ m), calculate the escape speed. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.69 × 10²⁴ / 8.28 × 10⁶) = 6.58 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 6.58 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a gas-giant moon pair along their line of centres, Major Moon (mass 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Minor Moon (mass 3.73 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.74 × 10⁶ m) have a centre-to-centre separation of 3.46 × 10⁸ m. At what distance from the centre of Major Moon along the line joining their centres is the resultant gravitational field strength zero?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 2.77 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 2.77 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: A spherical blackbody hot B-type Orion-association star catalogued by an ultraviolet sky survey radiates total power 3.359 × 10²⁸ W with spectral peak λ_max = 532.1 nm (b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴). Calculate its stellar radius.
items.workedSolution: By Wien's law, T = b / λ_max = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (532.1 × 10⁻⁹) = 5.45 × 10³ K. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 7.31 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds T = 5.45 × 10³ K via Wien's law and R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 7.31 × 10⁹ m.

items.stem: Assisted by lateral grip of static coefficient 0.35 on a banked oval speedway turn banked at 16 ° with radius 145 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²), a 320 kg endurance prototype sports car moves at 25.9 m s⁻¹. Find the maximum safe cornering speed.
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 16° + 0.35 cos 16°) / (cos 16° − 0.35 sin 16°)] = 31.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 31.7 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Along the line joining World P (mass 7.46 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and World Q (mass 1.19 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m) separated centre-to-centre by 4.03 × 10⁸ m, a 900 kg ballistic research capsule is at distance 2.22 × 10⁸ m from World P's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². What is the magnitude of the resultant gravitational field due to both bodies at the ballistic research capsule?
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.0101 − 0.00242| = 0.00767 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.00767 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Along the 3.84 × 10⁸ m line of centres of a terrestrial bi-planetary system, Planet Major (8.36 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Planet Minor (3.34 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) create a zero-field saddle point. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², find the total gravitational potential there.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.20 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -2.09 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -2.09 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A conical pendulum (0.75 kg, cord length 3.2 m) in an undergraduate mechanics laboratory revolves steadily with its cord inclined at 42 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the horizontal acceleration toward the centre of the circle.
items.workedSolution: Dividing horizontal Newton's second law T sin θ = m a_c by vertical equilibrium T cos θ = mg gives a_c = g tan θ = 9.81 × tan 42° = 8.83 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies a_c = g tan 42° to obtain 8.83 m s⁻².

items.stem: Sensors on an iced banked chute corner (radius 215 m, banking 25 °) measure the perpendicular load of a 640 kg bobsleigh cruising with zero side-friction. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the normal reaction.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (640 × 9.81) / cos 25° = 6.93 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 25° = mg to obtain N = 6.93 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular guide rail of radius 1.1 m shows a 0.9 kg instrumented acrylic sphere whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 5.19 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.9 × ((5.19)² / 1.1 − 9.8) = 13.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 13.2 N.

items.stem: Determine the scalar gravitational potential V_g (relative to zero at infinity) at a 460 kg gravimetry sonde positioned 1.16 × 10⁷ m from the centre of a Kepler-analog rocky super-Earth of mass 8.95 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 4.46 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 8.95 × 10²⁴) / 1.16 × 10⁷ = -5.15 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -5.15 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: Determine the radiant flux density b = L / (4πd²) received at a space-based spectrometer from a spherical blackbody luminous F-type subgiant of radius 3.83 × 10⁹ m and surface temperature 6250 K located 4.38 × 10¹⁶ m away (σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴).
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 4π R² σ T⁴ = 4π(3.83 × 10⁹)²(5.67 × 10⁻⁸)(6250)⁴ = 1.59 × 10²⁸ W. Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = σ T⁴ (R / d)² = 6.62 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses L = 4πR²σT⁴ and b = L / (4πd²) to obtain 6.62 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

items.stem: Calculate the road normal reaction on a 1350 kg vintage touring car cresting the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of radius 44 m at constant speed 17.9 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1350 × (9.81 − (17.9)² / 44) = 3.41 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 3.41 × 10³ N.

items.stem: A spherical charted extrasolar rocky world (mass 1.31 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 9.87 × 10⁶ m) is observed by a 620 kg magnetospheric probe at radial distance 3.16 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², at what minimum speed must an object leave the surface R to reach infinity?
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.31 × 10²⁵ / 9.87 × 10⁶) = 1.33 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 1.33 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Along the axis connecting Host World (1.07 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Icy Moon (2.97 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.74 × 10⁶ m) in a super-Earth and its captured icy satellite of separation 5.38 × 10⁸ m, locate the zero-field coordinate measured from the centre of Host World.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 4.61 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 4.61 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: Swinging steadily around a vertical axis in an overhead cable rig, a 1.2 kg suspended ice-arena tracking camera pod hangs from a 1.1 m tether inclined at 42 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is its speed along the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.1 sin 42° = 0.736 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.736 × tan 42°) = 2.55 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: On a canted main-line viaduct curve (radius 105 m, bank angle 28 °, μ_s = 0.25), a 1050 kg coach currently travels at 26.9 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the upper non-skidding speed limit.
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 28° + 0.25 cos 28°) / (cos 28° − 0.25 sin 28°)] = 30.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 30.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Moving at 8.08 m s⁻¹ over a convex circular ridge crest of circular radius 22 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²), what normal force supports a 1520 kg autonomous rover chassis at the crest?
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1520 × (9.8 − (8.08)² / 22) = 1.04 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 1.04 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: Determine the escape velocity from orbital radius r = 1.77 × 10⁷ m for a 1100 kg laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter orbiting a spherical silicate planet of mass 1.49 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 4.92 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Escape from radial distance r requires ½m v_esc² − GMm/r = 0, so v_esc = √(2GM / r) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.49 × 10²⁵ / 1.77 × 10⁷) = 1.06 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates circular orbital speed √(GM / r) and omits the √2 factor needed to escape from orbit.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies circular orbital speed by 2 instead of √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates escape speed from the planet's surface R_p rather than from the satellite's orbital radius r.

items.stem: From the airless surface of Primary Planet (mass 1.25 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m), a cislunar transfer probe is fired along the line of centres toward Companion Moon (mass 1.95 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) at separation 2.77 × 10⁸ m. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², determine the threshold launch speed to cross the null-point barrier.
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -1.14 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 2.46 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -3.81 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.10 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.48 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.48 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 1.2 kg wind-tunnel tethered aerodynamic probe attached to a 1.65 m light wire revolves in a horizontal circle inside a rotary calibration fixture at a constant semi-vertical angle of 24 °. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the time period of one complete revolution?
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((1.65 cos 24°) / 9.8) = 2.46 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 24° / g) to obtain 2.46 s.

items.stem: A 3.5 kg acrobatic drone tether pod revolves at a constant speed of 4.44 m s⁻¹ in a vertical circle of radius 1.35 m guided by a constant-speed vertical line. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both tension and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 3.5 × ((4.44)² / 1.35 − 9.81) = 16.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 16.8 N.

items.stem: A deep-shaft gravimeter of mass 900 kg is located at radial distance 3.15 × 10⁷ m from the centre of an airless synthetic uniform planetary body of mass 2.63 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 7.01 × 10⁶ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and potential to be zero at infinity, what is the gravitational potential at the deep-shaft gravimeter's position?
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.63 × 10²⁵) / 3.15 × 10⁷ = -5.57 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -5.57 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: A X-ray timing observatory of mass 1350 kg moves in a circular orbit of radius 3.3 × 10⁷ m around a central rocky exoplanet of mass 2.99 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 7.86 × 10⁶ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential energy at infinity. What is the total mechanical energy of the spacecraft in this orbit?
items.workedSolution: In a circular orbit, E_k = +GMm/(2r) and E_p = −GMm/r, so E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.99 × 10²⁴ × 1350) / (2 × 3.3 × 10⁷) = -4.08 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r) with negative sign to obtain -4.08 × 10⁹ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_tot = −GMm/(2r), quoting gravitational potential energy −GMm/r instead.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the negative bound-state sign, reporting +GMm/(2r) instead of −GMm/(2r).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits both the negative sign and the virial factor of 1/2, reporting +GMm/r.

items.stem: Thrusters boost a 1500 kg ocean-altimetry spacecraft around an Earth-mass rocky world (mass 6.14 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.54 × 10⁶ m) from a circular orbit of radius 1.21 × 10⁷ m to a higher circular orbit of radius 4.84 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². What minimum mechanical energy must the thrusters supply?

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔE_tot = ½GMm(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) to obtain 1.90 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reverses initial and final radii, obtaining a negative energy requirement for raising the orbit.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates |E_tot(r₂)| alone instead of subtracting initial total energy E_tot(r₁) from E_tot(r₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the gain in gravitational potential energy ΔE_p = GMm(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) and forgets the virial reduction in kinetic energy (factor of 1/2).

items.stem: Primary (mass 4.18 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Exomoon (mass 4.64 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) have a centre-to-centre separation of 3.35 × 10⁸ m in a sub-Neptune and its massive exomoon. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential at infinity. What is the combined gravitational potential at the collinear point where the resultant gravitational field is zero?
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.51 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -1.48 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -1.48 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Observations with a high-altitude observatory target a spherical blackbody yellow-white standard-candle star of radius 3.83 × 10⁹ m and effective surface temperature 9600 K situated 2.41 × 10¹⁶ m from the detector. Take σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. What apparent brightness (radiant intensity) arrives at the detector?
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 4π R² σ T⁴ = 4π(3.83 × 10⁹)²(5.67 × 10⁻⁸)(9600)⁴ = 8.88 × 10²⁸ W. Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = σ T⁴ (R / d)² = 1.22 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses L = 4πR²σT⁴ and b = L / (4πd²) to obtain 1.22 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻².

items.stem: Rounding a banked elevated beamway (radius 32 m, bank angle 28 °) with zero lateral friction, a 1420 kg shuttle stays in a horizontal circle. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², determine the normal reaction force.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (1420 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 1.58 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 1.58 × 10⁴ N.

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the horizontal centripetal force mg tan θ instead of the normal reaction mg / cos θ.

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates normal reaction to weight mg without accounting for the tilted surface.

items.stem: Orbiting a rocky central planet (mass 4.61 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.9 × 10⁶ m) along a circle of radius 8.85 × 10⁶ m, a ion-propelled communications relay has mass 1650 kg. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate the orbital kinetic energy of the spacecraft.
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.61 × 10²⁴ × 1650) / (2 × 8.85 × 10⁶) = 2.87 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative sign to kinetic energy by confusing E_k with total orbital energy E_tot.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

items.stem: During rotational testing in an inertial navigation testbed, a 1.8 kg reference mass on a 0.95 m tether describes a horizontal circle with the tether inclined at 24 ° to the downward vertical. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², calculate the tension force in the tether.
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (1.8 × 9.8) / cos 24° = 19.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 24° = mg to obtain T = 19.3 N.

items.stem: A 1750 kg alpine highway tour bus corners at 16.1 m s⁻¹ on a superelevated mountain bend of horizontal radius 58 m banked at 14 °, where the static friction coefficient is 0.4 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed at which it can round this banked turn without skidding outward?
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 14° + 0.4 cos 14°) / (cos 14° − 0.4 sin 14°)] = 20.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 20.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a vertical whirl boom of radius 0.65 m, a 0.75 kg aerospace g-tolerance capsule rotates vertically at 3.69 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², if the drive is slowed, at what critical apex speed does the tension vanish?
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, tension = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.81 × 0.65) = 2.53 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 2.53 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Between circular orbits of radii r₁ = 1.26 × 10⁷ m and r₂ = 2.52 × 10⁷ m around a uniform spherical planet (mass 1.1 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.72 × 10⁶ m), a 463 kg planetary gravity-mapping orbiter coasts along a tangent Hohmann transfer ellipse (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the transit time from periapsis to apoapsis.
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 1.89 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 9.53 × 10³ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 9.53 × 10³ s.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Takes half the outer circular period using r₂ instead of the transfer ellipse semi-major axis (r₁ + r₂)/2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full elliptical period 2π√(a³ / GM) instead of the half-orbit Hohmann coast time π√(a³ / GM).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses major axis (r₁ + r₂) instead of semi-major axis a = (r₁ + r₂)/2 in Kepler's third law.

items.stem: A conical pendulum in a frictionless swivel mast consists of a 1.8 kg steel sphere and a 1.25 m inextensible string making 38 ° with the vertical axis (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Determine the orbital speed of the steel sphere.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.25 sin 38° = 0.770 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.770 × tan 38°) = 2.43 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.43 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular stator ring of radius 1.6 m shows a 0.9 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 6.26 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.9 × ((6.26)² / 1.6 − 9.8) = 13.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 13.2 N.

items.stem: Determine the scalar gravitational potential V_g (relative to zero at infinity) at a 360 kg subsurface borehole sensor positioned 1.51 × 10⁷ m from the centre of a uniform-density silicate moon of mass 2.77 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 7.21 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.77 × 10²⁴) / 1.51 × 10⁷ = -1.22 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -1.22 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔE_tot = ½GMm(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) to obtain 6.03 × 10⁹ J.

items.stem: Along the axis connecting Primary (7.68 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Exomoon (4.8 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) in a sub-Neptune and its massive exomoon of separation 4.15 × 10⁸ m, locate the zero-field coordinate measured from the centre of Primary.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.32 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 3.32 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: Determine the radiant flux density b = L / (4πd²) received at a calibrated bolometric detector from a spherical blackbody young open-cluster A-type star of radius 3.95 × 10⁹ m and surface temperature 18000 K located 1.11 × 10¹⁶ m away (σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴).
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 4π R² σ T⁴ = 4π(3.95 × 10⁹)²(5.67 × 10⁻⁸)(18000)⁴ = 1.17 × 10³⁰ W. Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = σ T⁴ (R / d)² = 7.54 × 10⁻⁴ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses L = 4πR²σT⁴ and b = L / (4πd²) to obtain 7.54 × 10⁻⁴ W m⁻².

items.stem: Without relying on lateral tyre or rail grip, a 1950 kg solar-powered cruiser vehicle negotiates a banked desert test circuit of radius 165 m inclined at 14 ° to the horizontal (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find its speed.
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 165 × tan 14°) = 20.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 20.1 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: With negligible drag, a 0.36 kg low-friction maglev test sled sweeps through the bottom of a vertical circular guide ring (radius 0.463 m) at 6.1 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², calculate the normal contact force at the top of the circle.
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (6.1)² − 4(9.8)(0.463) = 19.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.36(19.1 / 0.463 − 9.8) = 11.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 11.3 N.

items.stem: Primary Planet of mass 9.21 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Companion Moon of mass 1.47 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 1.74 × 10⁶ m) form a Earth-analog planet and its rocky moon separated centre-to-centre by 4.74 × 10⁸ m. Calculate the distance from Primary Planet's centre to the collinear gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.39 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 3.39 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: In a Neptune–Triton-analog planetary pair separated by 2.85 × 10⁸ m between centres, Ice Giant has mass 1.07 × 10²⁵ kg (radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Retrograde Moon has mass 2.18 × 10²³ kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m). Referencing potential to zero at infinity and taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate V_g at the gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.49 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -3.27 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -3.27 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Suspended by a 2.4 m line in a rigid ceiling pivot, a 2.5 kg weight executes uniform horizontal circular motion at 38 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Select the magnitude of its centripetal acceleration.
items.workedSolution: Dividing horizontal Newton's second law T sin θ = m a_c by vertical equilibrium T cos θ = mg gives a_c = g tan θ = 9.81 × tan 38° = 7.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies a_c = g tan 38° to obtain 7.66 m s⁻².

items.stem: Determine the maximum speed before outward skidding for a 160 kg indoor athletics track runner (currently at 17.1 m s⁻¹) on a banked curve lane of radius 45 m, banking angle 25 °, and μ_s = 0.3 (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 25° + 0.3 cos 25°) / (cos 25° − 0.3 sin 25°)] = 19.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 19.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At orbital radius 2.5 × 10⁷ m outside a spherical host world (mass 1.16 × 10²⁵ kg, surface radius 8.08 × 10⁶ m), what threshold speed must a 741 kg navigation constellation spacecraft attain so its total mechanical energy reaches zero? Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: Escape from radial distance r requires ½m v_esc² − GMm/r = 0, so v_esc = √(2GM / r) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.16 × 10²⁵ / 2.5 × 10⁷) = 7.87 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates circular orbital speed √(GM / r) and omits the √2 factor needed to escape from orbit.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies circular orbital speed by 2 instead of √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates escape speed from the planet's surface R_p rather than from the satellite's orbital radius r.

items.stem: An Olympic track cyclist of mass 320 kg rounds a Siberian-pine velodrome banking of horizontal radius 72 m banked at 14 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 72 × tan 14°) = 13.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 13.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An unpowered pendulum impact bob of mass 0.514 kg enters the bottom of a full vertical circular arc of radius 4.32 m with speed 21 m s⁻¹. Mechanical energy is conserved; take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is its speed at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((21)² − 4 × 9.8 × 4.32) = 16.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 16.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A cryobot instrument package of mass 803 kg is located at radial distance 3.88 × 10⁷ m from the centre of an airless icy outer-system dwarf world of mass 9.21 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 1.02 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and potential to be zero at infinity, what is the gravitational potential at the cryobot instrument package's position?
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 9.21 × 10²⁴) / 3.88 × 10⁷ = -1.58 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -1.58 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: In a tidally locked binary rocky worlds, World P (mass 1.35 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and World Q (mass 3.75 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) have a centre-to-centre separation of 6.52 × 10⁸ m. At what distance from the centre of World P along the line joining their centres is the resultant gravitational field strength zero?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 5.59 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 5.59 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: Inside a fairground swing carousel, a 1.1 m suspension wire supports a 0.35 kg gondola whirling at a steady semi-vertical cone angle of 42 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the tangential speed of the gondola.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.1 sin 42° = 0.736 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.736 × tan 42°) = 2.55 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Rounding a superelevated guideway curve (radius 145 m, bank angle 28 °) with zero lateral friction, a 640 kg carriage stays in a horizontal circle. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², determine the normal reaction force.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (640 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 7.11 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 7.11 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 0.65 m at steady speed 3.38 m s⁻¹, a 3.5 kg instrumented acrylic sphere is constrained by a vertical circular guide rail (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward normal contact force.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward normal contact force opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 3.5 × ((3.38)² / 0.65 + 9.8) = 95.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 95.8 N.

items.stem: Orbiting a uniform spherical planet (mass 2.09 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 9.78 × 10⁶ m) along a circle of radius 4.11 × 10⁷ m, a planetary gravity-mapping orbiter has mass 1130 kg. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate the orbital kinetic energy of the spacecraft.
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.09 × 10²⁵ × 1130) / (2 × 4.11 × 10⁷) = 1.92 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative sign to kinetic energy by confusing E_k with total orbital energy E_tot.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

items.stem: A 2.1 m inextensible cord in a rotational test rig carries a 1.8 kg capsule around a horizontal circle with cone half-angle 24 °. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², find the orbital period.
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((2.1 cos 24°) / 9.8) = 2.78 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 24° / g) to obtain 2.78 s.

items.stem: At the summit of the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of vertical radius 14 m, a 1180 kg vintage touring car moves horizontally at 10.1 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Determine the normal force exerted by the surface.
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1180 × (9.81 − (10.1)² / 14) = 2.98 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 2.98 × 10³ N.

items.stem: In a test run on a polished vertical circular chute of radius 0.875 m, a 1.85 kg precision titanium sphere enters the bottom at 7.2 m s⁻¹ with negligible friction (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the minimum bottom entry speed that would still allow it to complete the full vertical loop without losing contact at the top?
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 0.875) = 6.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the net scalar gravitational potential (zero at infinity) at the collinear saddle point of zero field between Major Moon (4.42 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Minor Moon (1.77 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m), whose centres lie 5.89 × 10⁸ m apart (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 4.91 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -7.21 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -7.21 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: The blackbody continuum of a evolved red-clump giant (radius 1.51 × 10¹⁰ m, distance 5.23 × 10¹⁶ m) corresponds to an effective photospheric temperature of 5930 K as recorded by an astrometric space mission. Take Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K. At what wavelength, in nm, does its emitted spectrum peak?
items.workedSolution: Using Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / 5930 = 4.89 × 10⁻⁷ m = 489 nm.

items.stem: Sensors on an iced banked chute corner (radius 45 m, banking 28 °) measure the perpendicular load of a 880 kg bobsleigh cruising with zero side-friction. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the normal reaction.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (880 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 9.78 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 9.78 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Coasting without friction, a 1.85 kg gravity-fed capsule car passes the lowest point of a circular vertical inversion loop (radius 4.32 m) at 16.9 m s⁻¹ where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed as it crosses the apex.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((16.9)² − 4 × 9.81 × 4.32) = 10.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 10.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Orbiting an Earth-mass rocky world (mass 6.32 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.2 × 10⁶ m) at circular orbital radius 9.36 × 10⁶ m, a 1700 kg ocean-altimetry spacecraft is gravitationally bound. With E_p = 0 at infinity and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate its total mechanical energy.
items.workedSolution: In a circular orbit, E_k = +GMm/(2r) and E_p = −GMm/r, so E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 6.32 × 10²⁴ × 1700) / (2 × 9.36 × 10⁶) = -3.83 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r) with negative sign to obtain -3.83 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_tot = −GMm/(2r), quoting gravitational potential energy −GMm/r instead.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the negative bound-state sign, reporting +GMm/(2r) instead of −GMm/(2r).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits both the negative sign and the virial factor of 1/2, reporting +GMm/r.

items.stem: Ice Giant of mass 5.36 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Retrograde Moon of mass 6.62 × 10²² kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) form a Neptune–Triton-analog planetary pair separated centre-to-centre by 3.66 × 10⁸ m. Calculate the distance from Ice Giant's centre to the collinear gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: From the airless surface of Primary Planet (mass 7.27 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m), a cislunar transfer probe is fired along the line of centres toward Companion Moon (mass 2.02 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) at separation 2.92 × 10⁸ m. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², determine the threshold launch speed to cross the null-point barrier.
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -8.97 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 2.50 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -2.26 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 8.74 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.32 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.32 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Engineers operating a steam-turbine speed regulator spin a 0.75 kg governor mass suspended by a 0.95 m wire so that the wire makes a steady 20 ° angle with the vertical axis (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the tension supported by the wire.
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (0.75 × 9.8) / cos 20° = 7.82 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 20° = mg to obtain T = 7.82 N.

items.stem: Without relying on lateral tyre or rail grip, a 1050 kg autonomous mining haul truck negotiates a banked quarry spiral ramp of radius 105 m inclined at 14 ° to the horizontal (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find its speed.
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 105 × tan 14°) = 16.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 16.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At the nadir of a constant-speed vertical line (vertical radius 0.85 m), a 0.75 kg acrobatic drone tether pod travels horizontally at 4.97 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what tension acts upward?
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward tension opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.75 × ((4.97)² / 0.85 + 9.81) = 29.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 29.2 N.

items.stem: Determine the surface escape velocity for an unpowered projectile launched from a spherical charted extrasolar rocky world of mass 2.71 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 4.72 × 10⁶ m, given an exterior 370 kg magnetospheric probe at r = 9.91 × 10⁶ m and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.71 × 10²⁵ / 4.72 × 10⁶) = 2.77 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 2.77 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the translational kinetic energy of a 296 kg ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite in a circular orbit of radius r = 1.83 × 10⁷ m about an airless rocky planet (mass 6.32 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.3 × 10⁶ m, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 6.32 × 10²⁴ × 296) / (2 × 1.83 × 10⁷) = 3.41 × 10⁹ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative sign to kinetic energy by confusing E_k with total orbital energy E_tot.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

items.stem: Determine E_k(r₂) − E_k(r₁) when a 635 kg laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter orbiting a spherical silicate planet of mass 1.51 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 6.04 × 10⁶ m transitions from circular radius r₁ = 9.66 × 10⁶ m to r₂ = 2.32 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: Because E_k(r) = +GMm/(2r) decreases as r increases, ΔE_k = ½GMm(1/r₂ − 1/r₁) = -1.93 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = GMm/(2r).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Quotes the final kinetic energy E_k(r₂) rather than the change E_k(r₂) − E_k(r₁).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports a positive change +ΔE_k, overlooking that a higher circular orbit has a lower orbital speed and smaller kinetic energy.

items.stem: In a sub-Neptune and its massive exomoon separated by 3.54 × 10⁸ m between centres, Primary has mass 8.84 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Exomoon has mass 1.8 × 10²³ kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m). Referencing potential to zero at infinity and taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate V_g at the gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.10 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -2.17 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -2.17 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Inside a fairground swing carousel, a 1.25 m suspension wire supports a 3.2 kg gondola whirling at a steady semi-vertical cone angle of 38 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the tangential speed of the gondola.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.25 sin 38° = 0.770 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.770 × tan 38°) = 2.43 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.43 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Operators gradually reduce the speed of a 0.55 kg laboratory brass cylinder from 7.33 m s⁻¹ on an enclosed vertical circular hoop of vertical radius 1.6 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the minimum speed at the top before slackness or lift-off occurs.
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, normal contact force = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.8 × 1.6) = 3.96 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 3.96 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: For an unpowered 247 kg hardened steel ball bearing on a smooth vertical loop track of vertical radius 0.875 m (operating entry speed 8.39 m s⁻¹, g = 9.81 m s⁻²), find the least bottom speed needed so normal contact force does not vanish before the top.
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.81 × 0.875) = 6.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the unpowered coast duration along a Hohmann half-ellipse connecting r₁ = 1.76 × 10⁷ m to r₂ = 4.93 × 10⁷ m for a 825 kg ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite orbiting an airless rocky planet of mass 2.02 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 9.24 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 3.35 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 1.66 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 1.66 × 10⁴ s.

items.stem: A 0.75 kg wind-tunnel tethered aerodynamic probe attached to a 1.8 m light wire revolves in a horizontal circle inside a rotary calibration fixture at a constant semi-vertical angle of 20 °. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the time period of one complete revolution?
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((1.8 cos 20°) / 9.8) = 2.61 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 20° / g) to obtain 2.61 s.

items.stem: An proving-ground electric sedan of mass 1420 kg rounds a concrete parabolic test banking of horizontal radius 215 m banked at 16 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 215 × tan 16°) = 24.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 16°) to obtain 24.6 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Conserving mechanical energy throughout a vertical circular guide ring of radius 2.57 m, a 370 kg low-friction maglev test sled enters at the bottom with speed 15.1 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Determine the speed at the summit of the loop.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((15.1)² − 4 × 9.8 × 2.57) = 11.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 11.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Along the 5.01 × 10⁸ m line of centres of a Pluto–Charon-type dwarf-planet binary, Dwarf Planet A (1.1 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Companion B (1.22 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) create a zero-field saddle point. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², find the total gravitational potential there.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.76 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -2.60 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -2.60 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A 2.4 m tether in a steady slewing test guides a 0.85 kg ballast block around a horizontal circle at a steady cone half-angle of 42 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Find the inward radial acceleration of the ballast block.
items.workedSolution: Dividing horizontal Newton's second law T sin θ = m a_c by vertical equilibrium T cos θ = mg gives a_c = g tan θ = 9.81 × tan 42° = 8.83 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies a_c = g tan 42° to obtain 8.83 m s⁻².

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 0.85 m at steady speed 3.87 m s⁻¹, a 1.6 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled is constrained by a vertical circular stator ring (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward normal contact force.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward normal contact force opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 1.6 × ((3.87)² / 0.85 + 9.8) = 43.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 43.9 N.

items.stem: A spherical basaltic terrestrial planetoid (mass 4.42 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.72 × 10⁶ m) is observed by a 825 kg orbital transponder at radial distance 2.17 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², at what minimum speed must an object leave the surface R to reach infinity?
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.42 × 10²⁴ / 5.72 × 10⁶) = 1.02 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 1.02 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At centre-to-centre orbital radius 2.49 × 10⁷ m around a rocky central planet of mass 2.15 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 6.92 × 10⁶ m, find the orbital kinetic energy of a 762 kg ion-propelled communications relay. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.15 × 10²⁵ × 762) / (2 × 2.49 × 10⁷) = 2.19 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative sign to kinetic energy by confusing E_k with total orbital energy E_tot.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

items.stem: Comparing circular orbits of radii r₁ = 1.78 × 10⁷ m and r₂ = 6.41 × 10⁷ m around a spherical planetary body (mass 6.49 × 10²⁴ kg, surface radius 7.11 × 10⁶ m), find the signed change in orbital kinetic energy for a 1270 kg magnetospheric plasma observatory raised from r₁ to r₂ (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Because E_k(r) = +GMm/(2r) decreases as r increases, ΔE_k = ½GMm(1/r₂ − 1/r₁) = -1.12 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: Determine the least initial speed at Primary Asteroid's surface (1.32 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) enabling a ballistic ion-beam shepherd craft to reach Secondary Moonlet (8.25 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) across a 6.05 × 10⁸ m centre-to-centre baseline (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -1.38 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 4.84 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -2.27 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.36 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.65 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.65 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Observations by a stellar intensity interferometer yield bolometric luminosity L = 2.059 × 10³⁰ W and Wien peak wavelength 195.9 nm for a spherical blackbody bright southern-sky reference star. Taking b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, find R.
items.workedSolution: By Wien's law, T = b / λ_max = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (195.9 × 10⁻⁹) = 1.48 × 10⁴ K. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 7.76 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds T = 1.48 × 10⁴ K via Wien's law and R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 7.76 × 10⁹ m.

items.stem: In a test run on a full vertical circular arc of radius 0.635 m, a 0.212 kg pendulum impact bob enters the bottom at 8.48 m s⁻¹ with negligible friction (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the minimum bottom entry speed that would still allow it to complete the full vertical loop without losing contact at the top?
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 0.635) = 5.58 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 1590 kg planetary gravity-mapping orbiter around a uniform spherical planet (mass 1.16 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.19 × 10⁶ m) executes an elliptical Hohmann transfer with periapsis r₁ = 8.67 × 10⁶ m and apoapsis r₂ = 3.47 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². How long does the half-ellipse coast from r₁ to r₂ take?
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 2.17 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 1.14 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 1.14 × 10⁴ s.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Averages the inner and outer half-periods linearly rather than applying T ∝ a^(3/2).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full elliptical period 2π√(a³ / GM) instead of the half-orbit Hohmann coast time π√(a³ / GM).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses major axis (r₁ + r₂) instead of semi-major axis a = (r₁ + r₂)/2 in Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Between Primary Planet (mass 1.39 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Companion Moon (mass 3.86 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m), whose centres are 7.51 × 10⁸ m apart, find the combined gravitational field strength at a 978 kg cislunar transfer probe located 2.63 × 10⁸ m from Primary Planet's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.0134 − 1.08 × 10⁻⁴| = 0.0133 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.0133 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: In a vibration-isolated calibration bay, a ceiling-mounted metrology plummet of mass 0.35 kg hangs from an inextensible cord of length 0.8 m and sweeps a horizontal circle at a constant semi-vertical angle of 24 °. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in the cord?
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (0.35 × 9.8) / cos 24° = 3.75 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 24° = mg to obtain T = 3.75 N.

items.stem: An Olympic track cyclist of mass 82 kg rounds a Siberian-pine velodrome banking of horizontal radius 45 m banked at 16 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 45 × tan 16°) = 11.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 16°) to obtain 11.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Inside a fairground swing carousel, a 1.25 m suspension wire supports a 0.45 kg gondola whirling at a steady semi-vertical cone angle of 42 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the tangential speed of the gondola.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.25 sin 42° = 0.836 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.836 × tan 42°) = 2.72 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.72 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An unpowered 0.5 kg hardened steel ball bearing enters the bottom of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 1.6 m at 10.3 m s⁻¹ under energy-conserving conditions (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What normal contact force acts on it at the apex?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (10.3)² − 4(9.81)(1.6) = 43.3 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.5(43.3 / 1.6 − 9.81) = 8.63 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 8.63 N.

items.stem: Upon moving from a lower circular orbit of radius 1.32 × 10⁷ m to an outer circular orbit of radius 2.64 × 10⁷ m about a spherical terrestrial planet (mass 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.28 × 10⁶ m), calculate the signed kinetic energy change ΔE_k of a 450 kg synthetic-aperture radar satellite (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Because E_k(r) = +GMm/(2r) decreases as r increases, ΔE_k = ½GMm(1/r₂ − 1/r₁) = -3.39 × 10⁹ J.

items.stem: A 0.8 kg low-friction maglev test sled currently enters a vertical circular guide ring of radius 6.5 m at 21.8 m s⁻¹ under frictionless conditions (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the critical minimum speed at the bottom required to just clear the apex.
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 6.5) = 17.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A conical pendulum (0.75 kg, cord length 2.75 m) in an undergraduate mechanics laboratory revolves steadily with its cord inclined at 38 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the horizontal acceleration toward the centre of the circle.
items.workedSolution: Dividing horizontal Newton's second law T sin θ = m a_c by vertical equilibrium T cos θ = mg gives a_c = g tan θ = 9.81 × tan 38° = 7.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies a_c = g tan 38° to obtain 7.66 m s⁻².

items.stem: Sensors on an iced banked chute corner (radius 215 m, banking 28 °) measure the perpendicular load of a 880 kg bobsleigh cruising with zero side-friction. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the normal reaction.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (880 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 9.78 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 9.78 × 10³ N.
