items.stem: Determine the signed total orbital energy E_tot = E_k + E_p of a 720 kg ocean-altimetry spacecraft in a circular orbit of radius 2.4 × 10⁷ m around an Earth-mass rocky world of mass 1.13 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 9.24 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: In a circular orbit, E_k = +GMm/(2r) and E_p = −GMm/r, so E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.13 × 10²⁵ × 720) / (2 × 2.4 × 10⁷) = -1.13 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r) with negative sign to obtain -1.13 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_tot = −GMm/(2r), quoting gravitational potential energy −GMm/r instead.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the negative bound-state sign, reporting +GMm/(2r) instead of −GMm/(2r).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits both the negative sign and the virial factor of 1/2, reporting +GMm/r.

items.stem: Calculate the road normal reaction on a 1520 kg vintage touring car cresting the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of radius 44 m at constant speed 17.9 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1520 × (9.81 − (17.9)² / 44) = 3.84 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 3.84 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Climbing a full vertical circular arc of radius 1.2 m from a bottom speed of 10.4 m s⁻¹ without energy loss (g = 9.8 m s⁻²), what normal contact force does a 1.2 kg pendulum impact bob experience at the summit?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (10.4)² − 4(9.8)(1.2) = 61.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 1.2(61.1 / 1.2 − 9.8) = 49.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 49.4 N.

items.stem: A spherical charted extrasolar rocky world (mass 8.95 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.28 × 10⁶ m) is observed by a 620 kg magnetospheric probe at radial distance 2.65 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², at what minimum speed must an object leave the surface R to reach infinity?
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 8.95 × 10²⁴ / 8.28 × 10⁶) = 1.20 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 1.20 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Observations by a wide-field photometric survey yield bolometric luminosity L = 1.052 × 10²⁹ W and Wien peak wavelength 400 nm for a spherical blackbody metal-poor halo giant star. Taking b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, find R.
items.workedSolution: By Wien's law, T = b / λ_max = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (400 × 10⁻⁹) = 7.25 × 10³ K. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 7.31 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds T = 7.25 × 10³ K via Wien's law and R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 7.31 × 10⁹ m.

items.stem: Swinging steadily around a vertical axis in an overhead cable rig, a 1.2 kg suspended ice-arena tracking camera pod hangs from a 1.4 m tether inclined at 42 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is its speed along the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.4 sin 42° = 0.937 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.937 × tan 42°) = 2.88 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.88 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: On a canted main-line viaduct curve (radius 105 m, bank angle 25 °, μ_s = 0.25), a 1050 kg coach currently travels at 25.4 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the upper non-skidding speed limit.
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 25° + 0.25 cos 25°) / (cos 25° − 0.25 sin 25°)] = 28.9 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 28.9 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An unpowered precision titanium sphere of mass 120 kg enters the bottom of a polished vertical circular chute of radius 9 m with speed 31.9 m s⁻¹. Mechanical energy is conserved; take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is its speed at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((31.9)² − 4 × 9.8 × 9) = 25.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 25.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Rounding a banked elevated beamway (radius 32 m, bank angle 28 °) with zero lateral friction, a 1580 kg shuttle stays in a horizontal circle. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², determine the normal reaction force.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (1580 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 1.76 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 1.76 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: Moving without friction or propulsion, a 120 kg gravity-fed capsule car passes the lowest point of a circular vertical inversion loop (radius 0.85 m) at 7.1 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². Determine the normal contact force acting on it at the highest point.
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (7.1)² − 4(9.81)(0.85) = 17.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 120(17.1 / 0.85 − 9.81) = 1.23 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 1.23 × 10³ N.

items.stem: During rotational testing in an inertial navigation testbed, a 1.6 kg reference mass on a 0.95 m tether describes a horizontal circle with the tether inclined at 20 ° to the downward vertical. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², calculate the tension force in the tether.
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (1.6 × 9.8) / cos 20° = 16.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 20° = mg to obtain T = 16.7 N.

items.stem: Positioned in a circular orbit of radius 1.71 × 10⁷ m around a spherical terrestrial planet of mass 6.14 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 9.51 × 10⁶ m, a 288 kg synthetic-aperture radar satellite prepares a departure burn (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the local escape speed from r = 1.71 × 10⁷ m.
items.workedSolution: Escape from radial distance r requires ½m v_esc² − GMm/r = 0, so v_esc = √(2GM / r) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 6.14 × 10²⁴ / 1.71 × 10⁷) = 6.92 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates circular orbital speed √(GM / r) and omits the √2 factor needed to escape from orbit.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates escape speed from the planet's surface R_p rather than from the satellite's orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies circular orbital speed by 2 instead of √2.

items.stem: A conical pendulum in a frictionless swivel mast consists of a 2.5 kg steel sphere and a 1.1 m inextensible string making 38 ° with the vertical axis (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Determine the orbital speed of the steel sphere.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.1 sin 38° = 0.677 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.677 × tan 38°) = 2.28 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.28 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular stator ring of radius 1.35 m shows a 0.55 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 5.75 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.55 × ((5.75)² / 1.35 − 9.8) = 8.08 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 8.08 N.

items.stem: At the base of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 6.5 m, an unpowered 0.2 kg hardened steel ball bearing has horizontal speed 21.8 m s⁻¹. Neglecting resistive losses and taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², find its speed at the top of the loop.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((21.8)² − 4 × 9.81 × 6.5) = 14.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 14.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the scalar gravitational potential V_g (relative to zero at infinity) at a 360 kg subsurface borehole sensor positioned 1.79 × 10⁷ m from the centre of a uniform-density silicate moon of mass 2.77 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 8.52 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.77 × 10²⁴) / 1.79 × 10⁷ = -1.03 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -1.03 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: Without relying on lateral tyre or rail grip, a 82 kg solar-powered cruiser vehicle negotiates a banked desert test circuit of radius 190 m inclined at 16 ° to the horizontal (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find its speed.
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 190 × tan 16°) = 23.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 16°) to obtain 23.1 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: With negligible drag, a 0.36 kg low-friction maglev test sled sweeps through the bottom of a vertical circular guide ring (radius 0.617 m) at 7.04 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², calculate the normal contact force at the top of the circle.
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (7.04)² − 4(9.8)(0.617) = 25.4 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.36(25.4 / 0.617 − 9.8) = 11.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 11.3 N.

items.stem: Determine the translational kinetic energy of a 576 kg polar meteorological CubeSat bus in a circular orbit of radius r = 1.32 × 10⁷ m about a charted extrasolar planet (mass 1.16 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.06 × 10⁶ m, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.16 × 10²⁵ × 576) / (2 × 1.32 × 10⁷) = 1.69 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative sign to kinetic energy by confusing E_k with total orbital energy E_tot.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

items.stem: Suspended by a 2.75 m line in a rigid ceiling pivot, a 3.2 kg weight executes uniform horizontal circular motion at 38 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Select the magnitude of its centripetal acceleration.
items.workedSolution: Dividing horizontal Newton's second law T sin θ = m a_c by vertical equilibrium T cos θ = mg gives a_c = g tan θ = 9.81 × tan 38° = 7.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies a_c = g tan 38° to obtain 7.66 m s⁻².

items.stem: Determine the maximum speed before outward skidding for a 160 kg indoor athletics track runner (currently at 15.3 m s⁻¹) on a banked curve lane of radius 32 m, banking angle 28 °, and μ_s = 0.3 (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 28° + 0.3 cos 28°) / (cos 28° − 0.3 sin 28°)] = 17.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 17.6 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Operators gradually reduce the speed of a 0.9 kg motorized whirling calibration mass from 6.07 m s⁻¹ on a taut Kevlar cord of vertical radius 1.1 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the minimum speed at the top before slackness or lift-off occurs.
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, tension = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.8 × 1.1) = 3.28 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 3.28 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the unpowered coast duration along a Hohmann half-ellipse connecting r₁ = 1.08 × 10⁷ m to r₂ = 3.46 × 10⁷ m for a 978 kg polar meteorological CubeSat bus orbiting a charted extrasolar planet of mass 1.97 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 6.74 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 2.27 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 9.37 × 10³ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 9.37 × 10³ s.

items.stem: An Olympic track cyclist of mass 160 kg rounds a Siberian-pine velodrome banking of horizontal radius 85 m banked at 16 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 85 × tan 16°) = 15.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 16°) to obtain 15.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Thrusters boost a 1230 kg autonomous orbital servicing tug around a dense terrestrial world (mass 6.32 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.88 × 10⁶ m) from a circular orbit of radius 1.12 × 10⁷ m to a higher circular orbit of radius 4.03 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². What minimum mechanical energy must the thrusters supply?

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔE_tot = ½GMm(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) to obtain 1.67 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reverses initial and final radii, obtaining a negative energy requirement for raising the orbit.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates |E_tot(r₂)| alone instead of subtracting initial total energy E_tot(r₁) from E_tot(r₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the gain in gravitational potential energy ΔE_p = GMm(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) and forgets the virial reduction in kinetic energy (factor of 1/2).

items.stem: Inside a fairground swing carousel, a 1.25 m suspension wire supports a 0.25 kg gondola whirling at a steady semi-vertical cone angle of 38 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the tangential speed of the gondola.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.25 sin 38° = 0.770 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.770 × tan 38°) = 2.43 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.43 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Rounding a superelevated guideway curve (radius 145 m, bank angle 28 °) with zero lateral friction, a 320 kg carriage stays in a horizontal circle. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², determine the normal reaction force.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (320 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 3.56 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 3.56 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 0.65 m at steady speed 3.38 m s⁻¹, a 2.2 kg instrumented acrylic sphere is constrained by a vertical circular guide rail (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward normal contact force.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward normal contact force opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 2.2 × ((3.38)² / 0.65 + 9.8) = 60.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 60.2 N.

items.stem: A ballistic ballistic research capsule launches from the surface of World P (mass 1.59 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) directly toward World Q (mass 9.94 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m), whose centre lies 4.88 × 10⁸ m away (ignore rotation and atmosphere; G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). What minimum launch speed allows the ballistic research capsule to pass the gravitational null point and fall onto World Q?
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -1.67 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 3.90 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -3.40 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.63 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.81 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.81 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: How long does one full horizontal orbit take for a 0.45 kg sphere suspended on a 2.1 m tether inclined at 24 ° to the vertical in a guidance-sensor test chamber? Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((2.1 cos 24°) / 9.8) = 2.78 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 24° / g) to obtain 2.78 s.

items.stem: In a test run on a polished vertical circular chute of radius 0.875 m, a 1.23 kg precision titanium sphere enters the bottom at 7.2 m s⁻¹ with negligible friction (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the minimum bottom entry speed that would still allow it to complete the full vertical loop without losing contact at the top?
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 0.875) = 6.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 339 kg ion-propelled communications relay around a rocky central planet (mass 8.53 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.97 × 10⁶ m) executes an elliptical Hohmann transfer with periapsis r₁ = 1.99 × 10⁷ m and apoapsis r₂ = 3.18 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². How long does the half-ellipse coast from r₁ to r₂ take?
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 2.59 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 1.73 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 1.73 × 10⁴ s.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Takes half the outer circular period using r₂ instead of the transfer ellipse semi-major axis (r₁ + r₂)/2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full elliptical period 2π√(a³ / GM) instead of the half-orbit Hohmann coast time π√(a³ / GM).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses major axis (r₁ + r₂) instead of semi-major axis a = (r₁ + r₂)/2 in Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Sensors on an iced banked chute corner (radius 45 m, banking 25 °) measure the perpendicular load of a 1050 kg bobsleigh cruising with zero side-friction. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the normal reaction.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (1050 × 9.81) / cos 25° = 1.14 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 25° = mg to obtain N = 1.14 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: Engineers operating a steam-turbine speed regulator spin a 0.6 kg governor mass suspended by a 0.65 m wire so that the wire makes a steady 20 ° angle with the vertical axis (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the tension supported by the wire.
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (0.6 × 9.8) / cos 20° = 6.26 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 20° = mg to obtain T = 6.26 N.

items.stem: Without relying on lateral tyre or rail grip, a 1250 kg autonomous mining haul truck negotiates a banked quarry spiral ramp of radius 85 m inclined at 14 ° to the horizontal (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find its speed.
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 85 × tan 14°) = 14.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 14.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At the nadir of a constant-speed vertical line (vertical radius 0.65 m), a 0.75 kg acrobatic drone tether pod travels horizontally at 4.34 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what tension acts upward?
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward tension opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.75 × ((4.34)² / 0.65 + 9.81) = 29.1 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 29.1 N.

items.stem: Determine the surface escape velocity for an unpowered projectile launched from a spherical charted extrasolar rocky world of mass 3.81 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 4.72 × 10⁶ m, given an exterior 370 kg magnetospheric probe at r = 9.91 × 10⁶ m and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 3.81 × 10²⁵ / 4.72 × 10⁶) = 3.28 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 3.28 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Swinging steadily around a vertical axis in an overhead cable rig, a 0.85 kg suspended ice-arena tracking camera pod hangs from a 1.1 m tether inclined at 38 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is its speed along the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.1 sin 38° = 0.677 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.677 × tan 38°) = 2.28 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.28 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Operators gradually reduce the speed of a 0.9 kg laboratory brass cylinder from 7.33 m s⁻¹ on an enclosed vertical circular hoop of vertical radius 1.6 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the minimum speed at the top before slackness or lift-off occurs.
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, normal contact force = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.8 × 1.6) = 3.96 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 3.96 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: For an unpowered 123 kg hardened steel ball bearing on a smooth vertical loop track of vertical radius 0.617 m (operating entry speed 7.04 m s⁻¹, g = 9.81 m s⁻²), find the least bottom speed needed so normal contact force does not vanish before the top.
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.81 × 0.617) = 5.50 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a Pluto–Charon-type dwarf-planet binary of centre-to-centre separation 4.88 × 10⁸ m, a 2220 kg New-Horizons-class flyby craft crosses the line of centres 2.2 × 10⁸ m from Dwarf Planet A (7.89 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) toward Companion B (4.93 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m). Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate |g_net|.
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.0109 − 4.58 × 10⁻⁴| = 0.0104 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.0104 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A 0.75 kg wind-tunnel tethered aerodynamic probe attached to a 1.65 m light wire revolves in a horizontal circle inside a rotary calibration fixture at a constant semi-vertical angle of 20 °. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the time period of one complete revolution?
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((1.65 cos 20°) / 9.8) = 2.50 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 20° / g) to obtain 2.50 s.

items.stem: An proving-ground electric sedan of mass 1580 kg rounds a concrete parabolic test banking of horizontal radius 32 m banked at 16 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 32 × tan 16°) = 9.48 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 16°) to obtain 9.48 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Conserving mechanical energy throughout a vertical circular guide ring of radius 2.57 m, a 247 kg low-friction maglev test sled enters at the bottom with speed 15.1 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Determine the speed at the summit of the loop.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((15.1)² − 4 × 9.8 × 2.57) = 11.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 11.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 1950 kg alpine highway tour bus corners at 21.1 m s⁻¹ on a superelevated mountain bend of horizontal radius 120 m banked at 14 °, where the static friction coefficient is 0.25 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed at which it can round this banked turn without skidding outward?
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 14° + 0.25 cos 14°) / (cos 14° − 0.25 sin 14°)] = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a test run on a full vertical circular arc of radius 0.635 m, a 0.37 kg pendulum impact bob enters the bottom at 8.48 m s⁻¹ with negligible friction (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the minimum bottom entry speed that would still allow it to complete the full vertical loop without losing contact at the top?
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 0.635) = 5.58 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The blackbody continuum of a nearby M-dwarf flare star (radius 1.55 × 10¹⁰ m, distance 1.56 × 10¹⁶ m) corresponds to an effective photospheric temperature of 18400 K as recorded by a cooled CCD radiometer. Take Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K. At what wavelength, in nm, does its emitted spectrum peak?
items.workedSolution: Using Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / 18400 = 1.58 × 10⁻⁷ m = 158 nm.

items.stem: In a vibration-isolated calibration bay, a ceiling-mounted metrology plummet of mass 0.35 kg hangs from an inextensible cord of length 0.95 m and sweeps a horizontal circle at a constant semi-vertical angle of 24 °. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in the cord?
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (0.35 × 9.8) / cos 24° = 3.75 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 24° = mg to obtain T = 3.75 N.

items.stem: Inside a fairground swing carousel, a 1.4 m suspension wire supports a 0.35 kg gondola whirling at a steady semi-vertical cone angle of 38 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the tangential speed of the gondola.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.4 sin 38° = 0.862 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.862 × tan 38°) = 2.57 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.57 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 1.35 m at steady speed 4.87 m s⁻¹, a 0.9 kg motorized whirling calibration mass is constrained by a taut Kevlar cord (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward tension.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward tension opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.9 × ((4.87)² / 1.35 + 9.8) = 24.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 24.6 N.

items.stem: An unpowered 0.5 kg hardened steel ball bearing enters the bottom of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 1.2 m at 8.9 m s⁻¹ under energy-conserving conditions (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What normal contact force acts on it at the apex?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (8.9)² − 4(9.81)(1.2) = 32.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.5(32.1 / 1.2 − 9.81) = 8.48 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 8.48 N.

items.stem: From the surface of a non-rotating airless cratered terrestrial dwarf planet of mass 4.18 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 7.01 × 10⁶ m (monitored by a 240 kg polar radar surveyor at r = 1.23 × 10⁷ m), calculate the escape speed. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.18 × 10²⁴ / 7.01 × 10⁶) = 8.92 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 8.92 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Assisted by lateral grip of static coefficient 0.35 on a banked oval speedway turn banked at 14 ° with radius 120 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²), a 320 kg endurance prototype sports car moves at 22.5 m s⁻¹. Find the maximum safe cornering speed.
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 14° + 0.35 cos 14°) / (cos 14° − 0.35 sin 14°)] = 27.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 27.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Sensors on an iced banked chute corner (radius 215 m, banking 28 °) measure the perpendicular load of a 640 kg bobsleigh cruising with zero side-friction. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the normal reaction.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (640 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 7.11 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 7.11 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular guide rail of radius 1.1 m shows a 1.25 kg instrumented acrylic sphere whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 5.19 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 1.25 × ((5.19)² / 1.1 − 9.8) = 18.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 18.4 N.

items.stem: Determine the scalar gravitational potential V_g (relative to zero at infinity) at a 460 kg gravimetry sonde positioned 1.41 × 10⁷ m from the centre of a Kepler-analog rocky super-Earth of mass 6.57 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 6.57 × 10²⁴) / 1.41 × 10⁷ = -3.11 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -3.11 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: Comparing circular orbits of radii r₁ = 1.39 × 10⁷ m and r₂ = 4.45 × 10⁷ m around a spherical silicate planet (mass 1.43 × 10²⁵ kg, surface radius 5.57 × 10⁶ m), find the signed change in orbital kinetic energy for a 950 kg laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter raised from r₁ to r₂ (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Because E_k(r) = +GMm/(2r) decreases as r increases, ΔE_k = ½GMm(1/r₂ − 1/r₁) = -2.24 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = GMm/(2r).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Quotes the final kinetic energy E_k(r₂) rather than the change E_k(r₂) − E_k(r₁).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports a positive change +ΔE_k, overlooking that a higher circular orbit has a lower orbital speed and smaller kinetic energy.

items.stem: Swinging steadily around a vertical axis in an overhead cable rig, a 1.4 kg suspended ice-arena tracking camera pod hangs from a 1.1 m tether inclined at 38 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is its speed along the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.1 sin 38° = 0.677 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.677 × tan 38°) = 2.28 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.28 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the net gravitational field magnitude acting on a 2100 kg deep-space relay probe positioned at x = 2.85 × 10⁸ m from Ice Giant (1.07 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) along the 6.34 × 10⁸ m baseline to Retrograde Moon (8.73 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.00879 − 4.78 × 10⁻⁴| = 0.00831 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.00831 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: At the nadir of a rigid rotating arm (vertical radius 2.4 m), a 0.9 kg human-rated centrifuge gondola travels horizontally at 8.35 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what tension acts upward?
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward tension opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.9 × ((8.35)² / 2.4 + 9.81) = 35.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 35.0 N.

items.stem: Rounding a banked elevated beamway (radius 32 m, bank angle 25 °) with zero lateral friction, a 1420 kg shuttle stays in a horizontal circle. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², determine the normal reaction force.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (1420 × 9.81) / cos 25° = 1.54 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 25° = mg to obtain N = 1.54 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: Moving without friction or propulsion, a 120 kg gravity-fed capsule car passes the lowest point of a circular vertical inversion loop (radius 0.6 m) at 5.97 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². Determine the normal contact force acting on it at the highest point.
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (5.97)² − 4(9.81)(0.6) = 12.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 120(12.1 / 0.6 − 9.81) = 1.24 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 1.24 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Spectrometry from a stellar intensity interferometer shows that a blackbody bright southern-sky reference star has total bolometric luminosity 3.234 × 10²⁹ W and a blackbody spectrum peaking at wavelength 302.1 nm. Take Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. What is the radius of the star?
items.workedSolution: By Wien's law, T = b / λ_max = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (302.1 × 10⁻⁹) = 9.60 × 10³ K. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 7.31 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds T = 9.60 × 10³ K via Wien's law and R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 7.31 × 10⁹ m.

items.stem: During rotational testing in an inertial navigation testbed, a 2.2 kg reference mass on a 0.95 m tether describes a horizontal circle with the tether inclined at 20 ° to the downward vertical. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², calculate the tension force in the tether.
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (2.2 × 9.8) / cos 20° = 22.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 20° = mg to obtain T = 22.9 N.

items.stem: A 1580 kg alpine highway tour bus corners at 18.8 m s⁻¹ on a superelevated mountain bend of horizontal radius 72 m banked at 16 °, where the static friction coefficient is 0.4 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed at which it can round this banked turn without skidding outward?
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 16° + 0.4 cos 16°) / (cos 16° − 0.4 sin 16°)] = 23.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 23.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular stator ring of radius 1.6 m shows a 0.55 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 6.26 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.55 × ((6.26)² / 1.6 − 9.8) = 8.08 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 8.08 N.

items.stem: Operators gradually reduce the speed of a 1.25 kg motorized whirling calibration mass from 6.07 m s⁻¹ on a taut Kevlar cord of vertical radius 1.1 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the minimum speed at the top before slackness or lift-off occurs.
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, tension = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.8 × 1.1) = 3.28 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 3.28 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An Olympic track cyclist of mass 160 kg rounds a Siberian-pine velodrome banking of horizontal radius 85 m banked at 14 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 85 × tan 14°) = 14.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 14.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An unpowered pendulum impact bob of mass 0.514 kg enters the bottom of a full vertical circular arc of radius 6.69 m with speed 26.1 m s⁻¹. Mechanical energy is conserved; take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is its speed at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((26.1)² − 4 × 9.8 × 6.69) = 20.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 20.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A cryobot instrument package of mass 803 kg is located at radial distance 3.24 × 10⁷ m from the centre of an airless icy outer-system dwarf world of mass 9.21 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 8.52 × 10⁶ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and potential to be zero at infinity, what is the gravitational potential at the cryobot instrument package's position?
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 9.21 × 10²⁴) / 3.24 × 10⁷ = -1.90 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -1.90 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: Observations with an orbital bolometric photometer target a spherical blackbody blue-white main-sequence star Vega-analog of radius 3.95 × 10⁹ m and effective surface temperature 5580 K situated 4.5 × 10¹⁶ m from the detector. Take σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. What apparent brightness (radiant intensity) arrives at the detector?
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 4π R² σ T⁴ = 4π(3.95 × 10⁹)²(5.67 × 10⁻⁸)(5580)⁴ = 1.08 × 10²⁸ W. Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = σ T⁴ (R / d)² = 4.24 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses L = 4πR²σT⁴ and b = L / (4πd²) to obtain 4.24 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

items.stem: Inside a fairground swing carousel, a 1.25 m suspension wire supports a 4.5 kg gondola whirling at a steady semi-vertical cone angle of 38 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the tangential speed of the gondola.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.25 sin 38° = 0.770 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.770 × tan 38°) = 2.43 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.43 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Rounding a superelevated guideway curve (radius 120 m, bank angle 25 °) with zero lateral friction, a 320 kg carriage stays in a horizontal circle. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², determine the normal reaction force.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (320 × 9.81) / cos 25° = 3.46 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 25° = mg to obtain N = 3.46 × 10³ N.

items.stem: How long does one full horizontal orbit take for a 0.35 kg sphere suspended on a 2.1 m tether inclined at 20 ° to the vertical in a guidance-sensor test chamber? Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((2.1 cos 20°) / 9.8) = 2.82 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 20° / g) to obtain 2.82 s.

items.stem: At the summit of the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of vertical radius 18 m, a 1180 kg vintage touring car moves horizontally at 11.4 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Determine the normal force exerted by the surface.
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1180 × (9.81 − (11.4)² / 18) = 3.06 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 3.06 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Sensors on an iced banked chute corner (radius 45 m, banking 28 °) measure the perpendicular load of a 1050 kg bobsleigh cruising with zero side-friction. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the normal reaction.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (1050 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 1.17 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 1.17 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: Coasting without friction, a 1.85 kg gravity-fed capsule car passes the lowest point of a circular vertical inversion loop (radius 2.57 m) at 13 m s⁻¹ where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed as it crosses the apex.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((13)² − 4 × 9.81 × 2.57) = 8.26 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 8.26 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Engineers operating a steam-turbine speed regulator spin a 0.45 kg governor mass suspended by a 0.8 m wire so that the wire makes a steady 20 ° angle with the vertical axis (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find the tension supported by the wire.
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (0.45 × 9.8) / cos 20° = 4.69 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 20° = mg to obtain T = 4.69 N.

items.stem: Without relying on lateral tyre or rail grip, a 1050 kg autonomous mining haul truck negotiates a banked quarry spiral ramp of radius 85 m inclined at 14 ° to the horizontal (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find its speed.
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 85 × tan 14°) = 14.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 14.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At the nadir of a constant-speed vertical line (vertical radius 0.85 m), a 0.4 kg acrobatic drone tether pod travels horizontally at 4.97 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what tension acts upward?
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward tension opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 0.4 × ((4.97)² / 0.85 + 9.81) = 15.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 15.5 N.

items.stem: Determine the radius of a blackbody metal-poor halo giant star whose continuum emission peaks at 354.5 nm and whose bolometric luminosity measured via a wide-field photometric survey is 1.814 × 10²⁹ W. Use b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: By Wien's law, T = b / λ_max = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (354.5 × 10⁻⁹) = 8.18 × 10³ K. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 7.54 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds T = 8.18 × 10³ K via Wien's law and R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 7.54 × 10⁹ m.

items.stem: A 1.65 m inextensible cord in a rotational test rig carries a 2.2 kg capsule around a horizontal circle with cone half-angle 20 °. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², find the orbital period.
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((1.65 cos 20°) / 9.8) = 2.50 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 20° / g) to obtain 2.50 s.

items.stem: An proving-ground electric sedan of mass 1580 kg rounds a concrete parabolic test banking of horizontal radius 215 m banked at 14 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 215 × tan 14°) = 22.9 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 22.9 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Conserving mechanical energy throughout a vertical circular guide ring of radius 1.65 m, a 247 kg low-friction maglev test sled enters at the bottom with speed 12.1 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Determine the speed at the summit of the loop.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((12.1)² − 4 × 9.8 × 1.65) = 9.04 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 9.04 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in a double-planetesimal binary system — Body Alpha (9.47 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (1.52 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) — lie 5.69 × 10⁸ m apart between centres. How far from Body Alpha's centre do their gravitational fields cancel?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 4.06 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 4.06 × 10⁸ m.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the unsquared mass ratio M₁ / (M₁ + M₂) (barycentre formula) instead of the square-root field ratio √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).

items.stem: A spherical basaltic terrestrial planetoid (mass 2.85 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.72 × 10⁶ m) is observed by a 825 kg orbital transponder at radial distance 2.17 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², at what minimum speed must an object leave the surface R to reach infinity?
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.85 × 10²⁴ / 5.72 × 10⁶) = 8.15 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 8.15 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An unpowered frictionless coaster bogie of mass 0.2 kg enters the bottom of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 0.6 m with horizontal speed 5.96 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 3.46 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 2.04 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 5.42 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the frictionless coaster bogie as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the string tension acting on the frictionless coaster bogie at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: A autonomous orbital servicing tug of mass 320 kg initially orbits a dense terrestrial world (mass 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) in a circular orbit of radius r₁ = 7.57 × 10⁶ m. Propulsion burns transfer it into a higher coaxial circular orbit of radius r₂ = 1.21 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -8.42 × 10⁹ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -5.27 × 10⁹ J, so ΔE_tot = 3.15 × 10⁹ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 1.33 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial total mechanical energy of the autonomous orbital servicing tug in the orbit of radius r₁.
Determine the minimum mechanical energy that must be supplied to transfer the autonomous orbital servicing tug into the circular orbit of radius r₂.
Calculate the orbital period of the autonomous orbital servicing tug in the outer circular orbit of radius r₂.

items.stem: A spherical blackbody blue-white main-sequence star Vega-analog observed by an orbital bolometric photometer has surface temperature 5000 K, radius 3.83 × 10⁹ m, and lies at distance 1.08 × 10¹⁶ m from Earth. Take b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b/T = 580 nm. (b) L = 4πR²σT⁴ = 6.53 × 10²⁷ W. (c) Apparent brightness b_app = L/(4πd²) = 4.46 × 10⁻⁶ W m⁻².

items.stem: Engineers design a superelevated guideway curve with a horizontal curve radius of 72 m and banking angle 28 ° so that a 160 kg carriage corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 28° = mg gives N = 1.78 × 10³ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 28° = 835 N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 19.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the carriage.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the carriage.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 19.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Engineers testing rotational instrumentation in a guidance-sensor test chamber whirl a 0.6 kg sphere on the end of a 1.8 m tether. Throughout the motion, the tether makes a constant semi-vertical angle of 20 ° with the vertical axis. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 20° = (0.6)(9.8) gives T = 6.26 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 1.8 sin 20° = 0.616 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.48 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.61 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cord supporting the sphere.
workingSteps: Vertical force balance gives T cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear speed of the sphere along its horizontal circular path.
workingSteps: Horizontal radius r = L sin θ = 1.8 sin 20° = 0.616 m.
From T sin θ = m v² / r, v = √(g r tan θ) = 1.48 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period for one complete revolution of the sphere.

items.stem: Coasting without propulsion or drag, a 0.8 kg acrylic demonstration glider passes through the lowest point of a vertical lecture-bench loop (radius 0.45 m) at speed 6.01 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 4.30 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 25.0 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 4.70 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the acrylic demonstration glider as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the string tension acting on the acrylic demonstration glider at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: A 1200 kg scientific transit module coasts along the axis connecting Planet Major (mass 7.46 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Planet Minor (mass 2.98 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) in a terrestrial bi-planetary system of centre-to-centre separation 4.61 × 10⁸ m, crossing coordinate x = 2.86 × 10⁸ m from Planet Major's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.84 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 2.86 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00543 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 6.52 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 6.52 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the distance from the centre of Planet Major to the collinear point where the resultant gravitational field strength is zero.
workingSteps: At the null point, G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)².
Taking square roots gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.84 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant gravitational field strength when the scientific transit module is 2.86 × 10⁸ m from the centre of Planet Major.
workingSteps: |g| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = 0.00543 N kg⁻¹.

parts.prompt: State the magnitude of the resultant gravitational force on the 1200 kg scientific transit module at this point.

items.stem: In a steam-turbine speed regulator, a centrifugal flyball governor mass of mass 0.75 kg is suspended from a fixed ceiling pivot by a light inextensible cord of length 0.8 m. The governor mass moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle such that the cord maintains a steady angle of 20 ° to the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 20° = (0.75)(9.8) gives T = 7.82 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 0.8 sin 20° = 0.274 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 0.988 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 1.74 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

workingSteps: Vertical force balance gives T cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear speed of the governor mass along its horizontal circular path.
workingSteps: Horizontal radius r = L sin θ = 0.8 sin 20° = 0.274 m.
From T sin θ = m v² / r, v = √(g r tan θ) = 0.988 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period for one complete revolution of the governor mass.

items.stem: An autonomous mining haul truck of combined mass 1050 kg travels around a banked quarry spiral ramp of horizontal radius 58 m inclined at a constant banking angle of 16 ° to the horizontal. At the chosen design speed, zero lateral frictional force acts along the slope. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 16° = mg gives N = 1.07 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 16° = 2.95 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 12.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the truck.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the truck.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 12.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An unpowered skatepark test trolley of mass 45 kg enters the bottom of a smooth circular vertical cradle of radius 2.5 m with horizontal speed 15.9 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 12.4 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 2.34 × 10³ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 11.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the skatepark test trolley as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the skatepark test trolley at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: An airless spherical airless iron-core protoplanet has mass 1.31 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 3.19 × 10⁶ m. A reconnaissance craft of mass 780 kg is stationed at radial distance 1.21 × 10⁷ m from the planet's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and gravitational potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -2.74 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 2.34 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 1.21 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -5.63 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

items.stem: A ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite of mass 1200 kg initially orbits an airless rocky planet (mass 1.91 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 8.52 × 10⁶ m) in a circular orbit of radius r₁ = 1.19 × 10⁷ m. Propulsion burns transfer it into a higher coaxial circular orbit of radius r₂ = 4.28 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -6.42 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -1.79 × 10¹⁰ J, so ΔE_tot = 4.64 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 4.93 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

items.stem: Mission planners analyse ballistic transfers across a double-planetesimal binary system where Body Alpha (4.3 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (2.69 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) are separated by 3.95 × 10⁸ m between centres. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.16 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -1.13 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 4.39 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 9.37 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

parts.prompt: Show where the collinear gravitational null point lies by calculating its distance from the centre of Body Alpha.
workingSteps: Equating field magnitudes gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.16 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined gravitational potential at this null point.
workingSteps: V(x₀) = −G M₁ / x₀ − G M₂ / (d − x₀) = -1.13 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the minimum launch speed from the surface of Body Alpha along the line of centres required for a sample-return lander to reach Body Beta.
workingSteps: ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 4.39 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹; v_min = √(2ΔV) = 9.37 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a vertical-loop mechanics experiment, a 360 kg frictionless coaster bogie is launched horizontally at 10.3 m s⁻¹ into the base of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 1.6 m where friction is negligible (g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 6.59 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 6.23 × 10³ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 8.85 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the frictionless coaster bogie at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: Engineers design a banked steel turnaround with a horizontal curve radius of 105 m and banking angle 25 ° so that a 1750 kg train corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 25° = mg gives N = 1.89 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 25° = 8.01 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 21.9 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the train.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 21.9 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Engineers testing rotational instrumentation in a rotational test rig whirl a 2.2 kg capsule on the end of a 1.8 m tether. Throughout the motion, the tether makes a constant semi-vertical angle of 20 ° with the vertical axis. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 20° = (2.2)(9.8) gives T = 22.9 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 1.8 sin 20° = 0.616 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.48 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.61 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

Propulsion burns transfer it into a higher coaxial circular orbit of radius r₂ = 3.05 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the acrylic demonstration glider as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the acrylic demonstration glider at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: In a gas-giant moon pair along their line of centres, Major Moon (mass 1.1 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Minor Moon (mass 4.4 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m) are separated centre-to-centre by 5.54 × 10⁸ m. A gravimetric drift sonde of mass 2160 kg travels along the line joining their centres and passes through a point at distance 3.43 × 10⁸ m from the centre of Major Moon. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 4.62 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 3.43 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00558 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 12.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 12.0 N.

workingSteps: At the null point, G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)².
Taking square roots gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 4.62 × 10⁸ m.

workingSteps: |g| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = 0.00558 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: In a vibration-isolated calibration bay, a ceiling-mounted metrology plummet of mass 3.2 kg is suspended from a fixed ceiling pivot by a light inextensible cord of length 0.95 m. The plummet moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle such that the cord maintains a steady angle of 20 ° to the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 20° = (3.2)(9.8) gives T = 33.4 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 0.95 sin 20° = 0.325 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.08 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 1.90 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: In a circular orbit of centre-to-centre radius 2.18 × 10⁷ m around a terrestrial host planet (mass 2.09 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.06 × 10⁶ m), a 906 kg cryogenic infrared space telescope has E_p = 0 at infinity. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 2.90 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -5.79 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -2.90 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the cryogenic infrared space telescope in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the cryogenic infrared space telescope.
Determine the total mechanical energy of the cryogenic infrared space telescope.
workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -2.90 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: In a terrestrial bi-planetary system of centre-to-centre separation 4.06 × 10⁸ m, Planet Major (mass 1.29 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Planet Minor (mass 1.43 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) are modelled as airless non-rotating spheres with V_g = 0 at infinity (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.05 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -3.77 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 1.56 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.76 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

items.stem: Data from an ultraviolet sky survey for a spherical blackbody hot B-type Orion-association star situated 1.96 × 10¹⁶ m from the detector show a spectral peak at λ_max = 519.7 nm and received radiant flux density 8.135 × 10⁻⁶ W m⁻² (b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴).
items.workedSolution: (a) Wien's law gives T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (519.7 × 10⁻⁹) = 5.58 × 10³ K. (b) Inverse-square law gives L = 4π d² b_app = 3.93 × 10²⁸ W. (c) Stefan-Boltzmann law gives R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 7.54 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Converts nm to m and applies T = b / λ_max.
Rearranges L = 4π R² σ T⁴ for R.

items.stem: A 640 kg endurance prototype sports car rounds a banked oval speedway turn of horizontal radius 215 m inclined at 16 ° to the horizontal at a steady speed of 33.4 m s⁻¹. The coefficient of static friction on the slope is 0.45. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Frictionless design speed v_ideal = √(g r tan 16°) = 24.6 m s⁻¹. (b) Resolving parallel to the incline gives f_s = m((v²/r) cos θ − g sin θ) = 1.46 × 10³ N down the slope. (c) At limiting grip, v_max = √[g r (sin θ + μ_s cos θ)/(cos θ − μ_s sin θ)] = 42.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves centripetal acceleration and weight components parallel to the slope.
Applies limiting down-slope friction in horizontal and vertical force equations.

items.stem: Referenced to zero potential energy at infinity, the orbital energy diagram models a 1390 kg magnetospheric plasma observatory circling a spherical planetary body (mass 4.74 × 10²⁴ kg, surface radius 6.74 × 10⁶ m) at radius r = 1.01 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 2.18 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -4.35 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -2.18 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the magnetospheric plasma observatory in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the magnetospheric plasma observatory.
Determine the total mechanical energy of the magnetospheric plasma observatory.
workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -2.18 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: A 952 kg inter-moon cargo ferry coasts along the axis connecting Host World (mass 5.36 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Icy Moon (mass 7.54 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m) in a super-Earth and its captured icy satellite of centre-to-centre separation 3.05 × 10⁸ m, crossing coordinate x = 1.68 × 10⁸ m from Host World's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.22 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 1.68 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00999 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 9.51 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 9.51 N.

workingSteps: At the null point, G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)².
Taking square roots gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 2.22 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant gravitational field strength when the inter-moon cargo ferry is 1.68 × 10⁸ m from the centre of Host World.
workingSteps: |g| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = 0.00999 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: The diagram represents a 1.2 kg tower-crane suspended ballast block in a steady slewing test describing a horizontal circle while supported by a taut cord of length 2.4 m inclined at 42 ° to the vertical. Take gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 42° = (1.2)(9.81) gives T = 15.8 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 2.4 sin 42° = 1.61 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 3.77 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.68 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: An airless spherical Kepler-analog rocky super-Earth has mass 2.71 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 1.02 × 10⁷ m. A gravimetry sonde of mass 254 kg is stationed at radial distance 1.79 × 10⁷ m from the planet's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and gravitational potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -1.77 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 1.88 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 1.79 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -2.56 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

items.stem: A X-ray timing observatory of mass 476 kg initially orbits a central rocky exoplanet (mass 1.13 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.92 × 10⁶ m) in a circular orbit of radius r₁ = 9.69 × 10⁶ m. Propulsion burns transfer it into a higher coaxial circular orbit of radius r₂ = 1.94 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -1.85 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -9.25 × 10⁹ J, so ΔE_tot = 9.27 × 10⁹ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 1.96 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

items.stem: At distance 2.48 × 10¹⁶ m, a luminous F-type subgiant behaves as an ideal blackbody radiator whose emission peaks at 390.8 nm and delivers apparent brightness 4.36 × 10⁻⁶ W m⁻² to a space-based spectrometer. Use b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) Wien's law gives T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (390.8 × 10⁻⁹) = 7.42 × 10³ K. (b) Inverse-square law gives L = 4π d² b_app = 3.37 × 10²⁸ W. (c) Stefan-Boltzmann law gives R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 3.95 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Converts nm to m and applies T = b / λ_max.
Rearranges L = 4π R² σ T⁴ for R.

items.stem: An unpowered frictionless coaster bogie of mass 123 kg enters the bottom of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 12.9 m with horizontal speed 30.7 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 20.9 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 2.96 × 10³ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 25.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the frictionless coaster bogie at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in a asteroidal binary pair — Primary Asteroid (7.89 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Secondary Moonlet (8.77 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.74 × 10⁶ m) — lie 4.26 × 10⁸ m apart between centres while a 1690 kg ion-beam shepherd craft is located 1.49 × 10⁸ m from Primary Asteroid's centre along their joining line. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.19 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 1.49 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.0229 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 38.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 38.8 N.

items.stem: A 1250 kg intercity tilting express coach rounds a canted main-line viaduct curve of horizontal radius 165 m inclined at 25 ° to the horizontal at a steady speed of 33.6 m s⁻¹. The coefficient of static friction on the slope is 0.35. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Frictionless design speed v_ideal = √(g r tan 25°) = 27.5 m s⁻¹. (b) Resolving parallel to the incline gives f_s = m((v²/r) cos θ − g sin θ) = 2.57 × 10³ N down the slope. (c) At limiting grip, v_max = √[g r (sin θ + μ_s cos θ)/(cos θ − μ_s sin θ)] = 39.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves centripetal acceleration and weight components parallel to the slope.
Applies limiting down-slope friction in horizontal and vertical force equations.

items.stem: In a circular orbit of centre-to-centre radius 1.62 × 10⁷ m around a spherical silicate planet (mass 1.2 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.23 × 10⁶ m), a 444 kg laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter has E_p = 0 at infinity. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 1.10 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -2.19 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -1.10 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter.
Determine the total mechanical energy of the laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter.
workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -1.10 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: Mission planners analyse ballistic transfers across a double-planetesimal binary system where Body Alpha (8.84 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (1.38 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) are separated by 4.17 × 10⁸ m between centres. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.71 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -1.79 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 7.87 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.25 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

parts.prompt: Show where the collinear gravitational null point lies by calculating its distance from the centre of Body Alpha.
workingSteps: Equating field magnitudes gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.71 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined gravitational potential at this null point.
workingSteps: V(x₀) = −G M₁ / x₀ − G M₂ / (d − x₀) = -1.79 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the minimum launch speed from the surface of Body Alpha along the line of centres required for a sample-return lander to reach Body Beta.
workingSteps: ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 7.87 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹; v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.25 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Mission analysts model a non-rotating airless synthetic uniform planetary body of mass 2.85 × 10²⁴ kg and surface radius 1.22 × 10⁷ m, together with a 656 kg deep-shaft gravimeter at distance 3.9 × 10⁷ m from its centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -1.56 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 5.58 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 3.9 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -3.20 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.
