items.stem: Around an Earth-mass rocky world (mass 4.54 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.18 × 10⁶ m), a 1010 kg ocean-altimetry spacecraft is raised from an inner circular parking orbit of radius r₁ = 1.8 × 10⁷ m to an operational circular orbit of radius r₂ = 5.76 × 10⁷ m. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -8.50 × 10⁹ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -2.65 × 10⁹ J, so ΔE_tot = 5.84 × 10⁹ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 1.58 × 10⁵ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial total mechanical energy of the ocean-altimetry spacecraft in the orbit of radius r₁.
Determine the minimum mechanical energy that must be supplied to transfer the ocean-altimetry spacecraft into the circular orbit of radius r₂.
Calculate the orbital period of the ocean-altimetry spacecraft in the outer circular orbit of radius r₂.

items.stem: A spherical blackbody yellow-white standard-candle star observed by a high-altitude observatory has surface temperature 11900 K, radius 4.07 × 10⁹ m, and lies at distance 1.14 × 10¹⁶ m from Earth. Take b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b/T = 244 nm. (b) L = 4πR²σT⁴ = 2.37 × 10²⁹ W. (c) Apparent brightness b_app = L/(4πd²) = 1.45 × 10⁻⁴ W m⁻².

items.stem: Engineers design a banked elevated beamway with a horizontal curve radius of 58 m and banking angle 25 ° so that a 1750 kg shuttle corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 25° = mg gives N = 1.89 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 25° = 8.01 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 16.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the shuttle.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the shuttle.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 16.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Coasting without propulsion or drag, a 370 kg acrylic demonstration glider passes through the lowest point of a vertical lecture-bench loop (radius 6.69 m) at speed 26.1 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 20.5 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 1.95 × 10⁴ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 18.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the acrylic demonstration glider as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the acrylic demonstration glider at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: In an inertial navigation testbed, a gyroscopic reference mass of mass 1.2 kg is suspended from a fixed ceiling pivot by a light inextensible cord of length 0.95 m. The reference mass moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle such that the cord maintains a steady angle of 24 ° to the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 24° = (1.2)(9.8) gives T = 12.9 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 0.95 sin 24° = 0.386 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.30 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 1.87 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: Relative to zero potential at infinity, the gravitational potential curve of a spherical metal-enriched exoplanet (mass 6.95 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.76 × 10⁶ m) is sampled by a 952 kg atmospheric-skimming bus at radial coordinate 3.94 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -5.29 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 1.03 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 3.94 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -1.12 × 10¹⁰ J.

Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

items.stem: Engineers design a superelevated guideway curve with a horizontal curve radius of 72 m and banking angle 25 ° so that a 320 kg carriage corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 25° = mg gives N = 3.46 × 10³ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 25° = 1.46 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 18.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the carriage.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 18.1 m s⁻¹.

Hence, or otherwise, determine the escape speed from the surface of the dense extrasolar ocean world.
workingSteps: ½ m v_esc² + m V_surface = 0 => v_esc = √(−2 V_surface).

items.stem: Around a rocky central planet (mass 1.07 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m), a 600 kg ion-propelled communications relay is raised from an inner circular parking orbit of radius r₁ = 1.39 × 10⁷ m to an operational circular orbit of radius r₂ = 3.34 × 10⁷ m. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -1.54 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -6.41 × 10⁹ J, so ΔE_tot = 8.99 × 10⁹ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 4.54 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial total mechanical energy of the ion-propelled communications relay in the orbit of radius r₁.
Determine the minimum mechanical energy that must be supplied to transfer the ion-propelled communications relay into the circular orbit of radius r₂.
Calculate the orbital period of the ion-propelled communications relay in the outer circular orbit of radius r₂.

items.stem: Coasting without propulsion or drag, a 1.2 kg acrylic demonstration glider passes through the lowest point of a vertical lecture-bench loop (radius 0.45 m) at speed 6.01 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 4.30 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 37.5 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 4.70 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

items.stem: In a steam-turbine speed regulator, a centrifugal flyball governor mass of mass 0.75 kg is suspended from a fixed ceiling pivot by a light inextensible cord of length 0.95 m. The governor mass moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle such that the cord maintains a steady angle of 24 ° to the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 24° = (0.75)(9.8) gives T = 8.05 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 0.95 sin 24° = 0.386 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.30 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 1.87 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: Referenced to zero potential energy at infinity, the orbital energy diagram models a 880 kg ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite circling an airless rocky planet (mass 1.13 × 10²⁵ kg, surface radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) at radius r = 1.97 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 1.68 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -3.37 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -1.68 × 10¹⁰ J.

Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -1.68 × 10¹⁰ J.

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential at the surface of the airless iron-core protoplanet.
Hence, or otherwise, determine the escape speed from the surface of the airless iron-core protoplanet.
workingSteps: ½ m v_esc² + m V_surface = 0 => v_esc = √(−2 V_surface).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the 780 kg reconnaissance craft at r = 1.21 × 10⁷ m.

items.stem: Data from an infrared space observatory for a spherical blackbody cool K-type giant Aldebaran-analog situated 5.09 × 10¹⁶ m from the detector show a spectral peak at λ_max = 362.5 nm and received radiant flux density 1.911 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻² (b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴).
items.workedSolution: (a) Wien's law gives T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (362.5 × 10⁻⁹) = 8.00 × 10³ K. (b) Inverse-square law gives L = 4π d² b_app = 6.22 × 10²⁹ W. (c) Stefan-Boltzmann law gives R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 1.46 × 10¹⁰ m.

markScheme.criterion: Converts nm to m and applies T = b / λ_max.
Rearranges L = 4π R² σ T⁴ for R.

Show what total luminosity the star radiates by calculating L in watts.
Determine the radius of the star.
workingSteps: From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)].

items.stem: An proving-ground electric sedan of combined mass 1250 kg travels around a concrete parabolic test banking of horizontal radius 165 m inclined at a constant banking angle of 14 ° to the horizontal. At the chosen design speed, zero lateral frictional force acts along the slope. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 14° = mg gives N = 1.26 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 14° = 3.05 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 20.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the sedan.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the sedan.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 20.1 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in a asteroidal binary pair — Primary Asteroid (3.58 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Secondary Moonlet (5.03 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) — lie 7.1 × 10⁸ m apart between centres while a 412 kg ion-beam shepherd craft is located 3.91 × 10⁸ m from Primary Asteroid's centre along their joining line. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 5.16 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 3.91 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00123 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 0.508 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 0.508 N.

workingSteps: At the null point, G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)².

workingSteps: |g| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = 0.00123 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Mission analysts model a non-rotating airless basaltic terrestrial planetoid of mass 3.7 × 10²⁵ kg and surface radius 9.87 × 10⁶ m, together with a 154 kg orbital transponder at distance 1.38 × 10⁷ m from its centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -2.50 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 2.24 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 1.38 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -2.75 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in a double-planetesimal binary system — Body Alpha (6.14 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (6.82 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m) — lie 3.56 × 10⁸ m apart between centres while a 926 kg sample-return lander is located 1.25 × 10⁸ m from Body Alpha's centre along their joining line. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.67 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 1.25 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.0254 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 23.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 23.5 N.

items.stem: Referenced to zero potential energy at infinity, the orbital energy diagram models a 432 kg autonomous orbital servicing tug circling a dense terrestrial world (mass 6.14 × 10²⁴ kg, surface radius 6.55 × 10⁶ m) at radius r = 1.44 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 6.14 × 10⁹ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -1.23 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -6.14 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the autonomous orbital servicing tug in this circular orbit.

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the autonomous orbital servicing tug.

workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -6.14 × 10⁹ J.

items.stem: Two non-rotating airless spherical bodies in a asteroidal binary pair — Primary Asteroid of mass 7.07 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m, and Secondary Moonlet of mass 1.96 × 10²³ kg and radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m — have a centre-to-centre separation of 5.73 × 10⁸ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 4.91 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -1.12 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 8.61 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.31 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

items.stem: A 640 kg endurance prototype sports car rounds a banked oval speedway turn of horizontal radius 190 m inclined at 14 ° to the horizontal at a steady speed of 29.9 m s⁻¹. The coefficient of static friction on the slope is 0.45. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Frictionless design speed v_ideal = √(g r tan 14°) = 21.5 m s⁻¹. (b) Resolving parallel to the incline gives f_s = m((v²/r) cos θ − g sin θ) = 1.40 × 10³ N down the slope. (c) At limiting grip, v_max = √[g r (sin θ + μ_s cos θ)/(cos θ − μ_s sin θ)] = 38.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves centripetal acceleration and weight components parallel to the slope.
Applies limiting down-slope friction in horizontal and vertical force equations.

workingSteps: v_ideal = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 190 × tan 14°) = 21.5 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Resolving along the slope toward the bottom: f_s = m ((v² / r) cos θ − g sin θ).

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum speed at which the car can negotiate this banked curve without skidding.
workingSteps: v_max = √[g r (sin θ + μ_s cos θ) / (cos θ − μ_s sin θ)] = 38.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The diagram represents a 0.45 kg tethered brass pendulum bob in an undergraduate mechanics laboratory describing a horizontal circle while supported by a taut cord of length 3.2 m inclined at 42 ° to the vertical. Take gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 42° = (0.45)(9.81) gives T = 5.94 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 3.2 sin 42° = 2.14 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 4.35 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 3.09 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

parts.prompt: Calculate the ideal speed at which zero lateral friction would act along the banked slope.
At the actual speed of 33.4 m s⁻¹, calculate the magnitude of the static frictional force acting parallel to the slope.
workingSteps: Resolving along the slope toward the bottom: f_s = m ((v² / r) cos θ − g sin θ).

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum speed at which the coach can negotiate this banked curve without skidding.
workingSteps: v_max = √[g r (sin θ + μ_s cos θ) / (cos θ − μ_s sin θ)] = 39.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Engineers design a banked elevated beamway with a horizontal curve radius of 72 m and banking angle 28 ° so that a 1580 kg shuttle corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 28° = mg gives N = 1.76 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 28° = 8.24 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 19.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the shuttle.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the shuttle.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 19.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Coasting without propulsion or drag, a 370 kg acrylic demonstration glider passes through the lowest point of a vertical lecture-bench loop (radius 9.26 m) at speed 30.7 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 24.1 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 1.95 × 10⁴ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 21.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the acrylic demonstration glider at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: In an inertial navigation testbed, a gyroscopic reference mass of mass 1.4 kg is suspended from a fixed ceiling pivot by a light inextensible cord of length 0.8 m. The reference mass moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle such that the cord maintains a steady angle of 24 ° to the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 24° = (1.4)(9.8) gives T = 15.0 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 0.8 sin 24° = 0.325 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.19 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 1.72 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: Relative to zero potential at infinity, the gravitational potential curve of a spherical metal-enriched exoplanet (mass 6.95 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.04 × 10⁷ m) is sampled by a 952 kg atmospheric-skimming bus at radial coordinate 4.68 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -4.46 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 9.44 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 4.68 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -9.43 × 10⁹ J.

items.stem: An unpowered frictionless coaster bogie of mass 0.35 kg enters the bottom of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 0.45 m with horizontal speed 5.17 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 3.01 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 3.64 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 4.70 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Equating field magnitudes gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 2.61 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined gravitational potential at this null point.
workingSteps: V(x₀) = −G M₁ / x₀ − G M₂ / (d − x₀) = -1.81 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

workingSteps: ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 5.76 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹; v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.07 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Engineers testing rotational instrumentation in a guidance-sensor test chamber whirl a 0.6 kg sphere on the end of a 2.1 m tether. Throughout the motion, the tether makes a constant semi-vertical angle of 24 ° with the vertical axis. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 24° = (0.6)(9.8) gives T = 6.44 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 2.1 sin 24° = 0.854 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.93 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.78 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: Mission analysts model a non-rotating airless dense extrasolar ocean world of mass 6.57 × 10²⁴ kg and surface radius 1.4 × 10⁷ m, together with a 350 kg telemetry buoy at distance 2.94 × 10⁷ m from its centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -3.13 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 7.91 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 2.94 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -5.22 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

items.stem: Coasting without propulsion or drag, a 0.8 kg acrylic demonstration glider passes through the lowest point of a vertical lecture-bench loop (radius 12.5 m) at speed 31.7 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 22.7 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 25.1 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 24.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the string tension acting on the acrylic demonstration glider at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 10.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a gas-giant moon pair along their line of centres of centre-to-centre separation 5.57 × 10⁸ m, Major Moon (mass 1.25 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Minor Moon (mass 2.55 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) are modelled as airless non-rotating spheres with V_g = 0 at infinity (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 4.87 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -1.95 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 1.29 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.61 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

items.stem: In a vertical-loop mechanics experiment, a 240 kg frictionless coaster bogie is launched horizontally at 12.8 m s⁻¹ into the base of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 2.5 m where friction is negligible (g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 8.11 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 3.97 × 10³ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 11.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: Engineers testing rotational instrumentation in a rotational test rig whirl a 2.5 kg capsule on the end of a 1.65 m tether. Throughout the motion, the tether makes a constant semi-vertical angle of 24 ° with the vertical axis. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 24° = (2.5)(9.8) gives T = 26.8 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 1.65 sin 24° = 0.671 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.71 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.46 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: An airless spherical Kepler-analog rocky super-Earth has mass 2.71 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 1.18 × 10⁷ m. A gravimetry sonde of mass 254 kg is stationed at radial distance 2.07 × 10⁷ m from the planet's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and gravitational potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -1.53 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 1.75 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 2.07 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -2.22 × 10¹⁰ J.

workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the shuttle.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 17.4 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Vertical force balance gives T cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear speed of the reference mass along its horizontal circular path.
workingSteps: Horizontal radius r = L sin θ = 0.65 sin 20° = 0.222 m.
From T sin θ = m v² / r, v = √(g r tan θ) = 0.890 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period for one complete revolution of the reference mass.

items.stem: Relative to zero potential at infinity, the gravitational potential curve of a spherical metal-enriched exoplanet (mass 4.42 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.76 × 10⁶ m) is sampled by a 952 kg atmospheric-skimming bus at radial coordinate 3.94 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -3.37 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 8.20 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 3.94 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -7.12 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

Hence, or otherwise, determine the escape speed from the surface of the metal-enriched exoplanet.
workingSteps: ½ m v_esc² + m V_surface = 0 => v_esc = √(−2 V_surface).
